Tenure-Track Faculty Recruitment (Open Rank)
University of California Los Angeles
Requisition Number: JPF11279
The Department of Physiology invites candidates for an open rank tenure-track faculty position in all areas of modern physiology.
The Department of Physiology at UCLA has a strong tradition of excellence in biophysics, membrane transport, neuroscience, cardiovascular research, and structural biology and has made many major discoveries in these areas. We welcome candidates investigating fundamental mechanisms across all areas of modern physiology, from molecular and cellular processes to organ and systems biology. Applications are also encouraged from researchers applying modern analytical tools, including data science, multi-omics, or advanced imaging, to address high-impact questions in biomedical science. Candidates must have a Ph.D., M.D., or equivalent degree, and are expected to have a strong track record of research achievements and a demonstrated interest in tackling outstanding biological problems using state-of-the-art approaches.
The successful candidate will be expected to develop an independent research program and participate in the teaching mission of the Department for medical, dental, and graduate students. We welcome candidates whose experience in teaching, research, or community service has prepared them to contribute to our commitment to inclusiveness and excellence.
For more information about the department, please visit the Physiology Department Website. Competitive start-up packages are available, along with lab and personal relocation allowances. Interested applicants should submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae, brief statement of research interests and career goals, description of teaching experience, and three letters of reference to UCLA Academic RECRUIT. Applications will be accepted between September 15 and November 15, 2026. Candidates who advance to the Short List must be available for on-campus interviews that will take place on January 21-22, 2027.
The University of California is committed to creating and maintaining a community dedicated to the advancement, application, and transmission of knowledge and creative endeavors through academic excellence, where all individuals who participate in University programs and activities can work and learn together in a safe and secure environment, free of violence, harassment, bullying and other demeaning behavior, discrimination, exploitation, or intimidation. With this commitment as well as a commitment to addressing all forms of academic misconduct, UCLA conducts targeted employment reference checks for finalists to whom departments or other hiring units would like to extend formal offers of appointment into Academic Senate faculty positions. The targeted employment reference checks involve contacting the finalists' current and prior places of employment to ask whether there have been substantiated findings of misconduct that would violate the University's Faculty Code of Conduct. To implement this process, UCLA requires all applicants for Academic Senate faculty positions to complete, sign, and upload the form entitled "Authorization to Release Information" into RECRUIT as part of their application. If the applicant does not include the signed authorization to release information with the application materials, the application will be considered incomplete. As with any incomplete application, the application will not receive further consideration. Although all applicants for faculty recruitments must complete the entire application, only finalists (i.e., those to whom the department or other hiring unit would like to extend a formal offer) considered for Academic Senate faculty positions will be subject to targeted employment reference checks.

We seek a physician who will help the Department achieve our goal of working with community partners to develop clinical, educational and research initiatives that revolutionize how people get and stay mentally healthy in Central Texas and beyond. Student loan forgiveness is available for faculty of the Department of Psychiatry through the Texas Mental Health Professionals Loan Repayment Program.
Additionally, DMS is a Health Research Institute (HRI) of the Texas Child Mental Health Care Consortium. The program and projects of the DMS HRI work to address the clinical needs of the programs which address urgent mental health challenges and improve the mental health care system in Texas for children, adolescents and their families. This position will provide clinical and consultative care as a part of the Child and Perinatal Psychiatric Access Network (CPAN and PeriPAN), a telephone consultation line for physicians, Texas Child Health Access through Telemedicine (TCHATT), a school-based telehealth program and Child Psychiatry Workforce Expansion (CWPE) projects for the Central Texas catchment area. We are also integrated in our local mental health community clinics.
Primary responsibilities will include providing clinical expertise to evaluate and treat a broad spectrum of mental health challenges for children and adolescents and in support of physicians who call the Child and Perinatal Psychiatric Access Network for consultation. The physician would also provide psychiatric care to children and adolescents as part of the Community Psychiatry Workforce Expansion (CPWE) program. This program is part of recent legislative funding to increase access to pediatric mental health services across Texas.
We seek candidates committed to providing exemplary care and treatment that restores hope and helps patients live healthier, fuller lives. A clinical assignment will occur through our Department's collaborations with the Seton Healthcare Family with the physician providing clinical care at a Local Mental Health Authority and/or Dell Children's Medical Center remotely.

Treatment and Assessment: Leveraging knowledge and understanding of child/adolescent psychiatry, treats and assesses patients and/or physicians (e.g., primary care physicians, family medicine doctors, etc.); obtains information through the clinical interview and interprets age-specific responses to treatment; leverages knowledge and understanding of psychosocial systems on treatment and age specific psychopharmacology to the benefit of the patient. Offers education, clinical recommendations, and referral information to equip doctors to manage mental health cases in the primary care setting. Treats patients, staff, and doctors with dignity and respect. Meets productivity standards as developed by the Medical Director. Prescribes medication in collaboration with the patient/guardian based on diagnosis and target symptoms, and in compliance with any applicable center formulary. Applies cost/benefit/risk analysis. Accounts for other medical conditions in making medical decisions and collaborates with other professionals as necessary. Complies with procedures for acquisition of medication through patient assistance programs. Provides ongoing in person and/or telemedical medication management services consistent with the standard of care and in accordance with applicable guidelines. Evaluates and monitors effectiveness and tolerability of psychiatric medications. Provides patient education and ensures appropriate consents are obtained. Performs AIMS and other assessments as applicable.
Evaluation: Provides and appropriately documents in person and/or telemedical psychiatric evaluations consistent with the standard of care and in accordance with any applicable guidelines and documentation requirements. Psychiatric diagnosis is supported by clinical findings. Orders lab work as indicated by patient need and in compliance with applicable rules and guidelines. Reviews lab results in a timely manner, and adjusts treatment as indicated.
Documentation: Documents all services in a professional and timely manner, using approved medical records systems and forms. Documents all services within 24 hours of service delivery including the addition of all documents and pertinent information between appointments, including phone calls, medication changes, and referrals. Clearly documents rationale for treatment that deviates from usual standards, such as polypharmacy, treatment of patients with ongoing substance use, use of off label medications, change in frequency of lab monitoring, long term use of benzodiazepines.
Emergency Evaluation: Provides child and adolescent psychiatric emergency evaluations and ongoing crisis services. Documents risk factors and recommendations. Assists staff in developing appropriate crisis plans.
Participates in treatment team meetings as indicated. Attends and participates in medical staff meetings, peer review, quality management activities, and other activities within the scope of a Child and Adolescent Psychiatrist and as assigned by the Medical Director. Sustains and cultivates team working relationships, and effectively collaborates with treatment team members. Collaborates with colleagues in the development of new services/programs/affiliations. Works with clinic staff to maximize access to psychiatric services and promotes efficiency and cost effectiveness of services

The University of Rhode Island College of Pharmacy invites applications for a full-time, academic-year (9-month), non-tenure-track Clinical Assistant Professor position in the Department of Pharmacy Practice and Clinical Research. The position will contribute to the College's teaching, clinical practice, service, and scholarly missions, with primary teaching responsibilities in the Pharmacy Practice and Care Process (PPCP)/Integrated Pharmacy Laboratory (IPL) sequence, Capstone courses, and other clinical courses within the Doctor of Pharmacy curriculum as needed.
The successful candidate will establish and maintain a clinical practice site in a clinic or ambulatory care setting that supports the expansion of pharmacist-provided patient care services, particularly for rural, underserved, and marginalized populations. The faculty member will also engage in service to the Department, College, University, profession, and community and pursue scholarly activities related to clinical practice, pharmacy education, community engagement, health disparities, or other areas aligned with the faculty member's expertise and interests.
The anticipated start date is September 1, 2026. This is a full-time, academic year, non-tenure-track, limited, renewable appointment, with continuation contingent upon successful performance review and programmatic needs.
KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
Teaching and Mentorship
Deliver instruction and facilitate active learning in the Pharmacy Practice and Care Process (PPCP)/Integrated Pharmacy Laboratory (IPL) sequence (I-V).
Lead and support skills-based education, including patient counseling and communication, prescription processing and clinical decision-making, drug information and medication therapy management, sterile and non-sterile compounding, physical assessment, and point-of-care skills.
Contribute to Capstone courses through case-based instruction, simulation activities, student assessment, course coordination, and activities designed to prepare students for Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experiences (APPEs) and contemporary pharmacy practice.
Deliver instruction in other required and elective clinical courses within the Doctor of Pharmacy curriculum based on departmental and programmatic needs and the faculty member's areas of expertise.
Facilitate recitations, simulations, case-based learning activities, and interprofessional education experiences.
Assess student performance through skills-based assessments, Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCEs), written assignments, care plans, and other appropriate assessment methods.
Provide timely feedback, remediation, coaching, and mentorship to support student development and professional growth.
Contribute to course and curricular assessment, continuous quality improvement, and curriculum development.
Oversee and mentor Teaching Assistants, pharmacy residents, and other learners assigned to relevant courses and educational activities.
Precept Doctor of Pharmacy students completing experiential education rotations.
Clinical Practice and Professional Service
Establish and maintain a high-quality clinical practice site in collaboration with a partnering clinic or healthcare organization.
Develop, implement, and evaluate pharmacist-provided patient care services designed to improve medication use, health outcomes, and access to care.
Provide direct patient care services within the scope of pharmacist practice and applicable state laws and regulations.
Collaborate with physicians, pharmacists, nurses, social workers, community health workers, and other healthcare professionals to provide patient-centered, team-based care.
Support initiatives designed to expand access to pharmacist-provided services for rural, underserved, marginalized, and other populations experiencing barriers to healthcare.
Develop a clinical practice environment that provides opportunities for student pharmacists, pharmacy residents, and other health professions learners.
Contribute professional expertise to community organizations, healthcare partners, professional associations, and other external stakeholders as appropriate.
Scholarship
Develop and maintain a program of scholarly activity consistent with the expectations of a non-tenure-track Clinical Assistant Professor.
Pursue internal and external funding opportunities to support clinical practice innovation, pharmacy education, community-engaged initiatives, healthcare access, health equity, or other areas aligned with the faculty member's expertise and interests.
Disseminate scholarly work through peer-reviewed publications, professional presentations, reports, educational scholarship, or other appropriate scholarly products.
Collaborate with faculty, students, healthcare professionals, and community partners on scholarly and grant-funded initiatives.
College, University, and Professional Service
Participate in departmental, College, and University governance and service activities, including appointment to standing and ad hoc committees.
Contribute to curriculum development, assessment, accreditation activities, and continuous quality improvement initiatives.
Participate in faculty meetings, strategic planning activities, student recruitment, and other activities supporting the missions of the Department and College.
Engage in service to professional organizations, healthcare organizations, community partners, or other external organizations as appropriate.
Collaborate with faculty, staff, students, and external partners to advance the teaching, practice, service, and scholarly missions of the College.

Perform other duties as assigned.

The incumbent is not substantially exposed to adverse environmental conditions.

4. Licensed or eligible for pharmacist licensure in Rhode Island.

From the Upstate to the Lowcountry, the University of South Carolina system is transforming the lives of South Carolinians through the impact of our eight institutions and 20 locations throughout the state. More than 50,000 students are enrolled at one of eight institutions, including the research campus in Columbia and comprehensive four-year universities in Aiken, Upstate and Beaufort. Advertised Job Summary:
Tenure-Track Assistant or Associate Professor in Food is MedicineThe Department of Health Promotion, Education, and Behavior (HPEB) at the University of South Carolina (USC) Arnold School of Public Health invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor or Associate Professor. This is a 9-month position.We seek a scholar whose research focuses on Food is Medicine, broadly defined as the integration of food- and nutrition-based interventions into health care and community settings to prevent, manage, or treat diet-related chronic disease and improve population health. Areas of interest may include, but are not limited to, medically tailored meals or groceries, produce prescription programs, nutrition screening and referral systems, food insecurity interventions, nutrition incentive programs, community-clinical linkages, or policies and payment models that support the integration of nutrition services into health care.The successful candidate will complement and expand existing departmental expertise in nutrition, healthy eating, behavioral interventions, implementation science, health economics, health communication, community-engaged research, global health, and health equity. We are particularly interested in candidates whose work addresses the implementation, evaluation, dissemination, or scaling of Food is Medicine programs and policies in real-world settings. Research that generates knowledge to help address the needs of rural, underserved, or historically marginalized populations, including communities in South Carolina and the broader Southeastern United States, is especially relevant to this position.The successful candidate will be expected to develop and maintain a robust, extramurally funded program of Food is Medicine research; publish findings in peer-reviewed outlets; contribute to undergraduate and graduate teaching in both in-person and online formats; and mentor master’s and doctoral students. The candidate will also be expected to collaborate across disciplines and with community, health care, governmental, and other external partners to develop, evaluate, implement, and scale effective Food is Medicine programs and policies.
The Department of Health Promotion, Education, and Behavior emphasizes both impactful research and meaningful community engagement. Faculty members examine how policy, environmental, institutional, health care, community, and individual factors influence health and work collaboratively to reduce health disparities and improve health outcomes for all. HPEB faculty members conduct research in areas including nutrition and healthy eating, implementation science, community-based research, health communication, global health, health services use, chronic disease prevention, and the translation of interventions into practice and policy. This position will strengthen the Department’s capacity to advance Food is Medicine research and develop collaborations among health care systems, community organizations, public agencies, food and nutrition assistance programs, and other partners.USC provides a rich interdisciplinary environment, with faculty across the Arnold School of Public Health and campus contributing to initiatives such as the Global Health Initiative, Nutrition Consortium, Prevention Research Center, Office for the Study of Aging, Consortium for Latino Health Studies, Big Data Health Science Center, and SmartState Centers. Opportunities also exist to collaborate with health care systems, state agencies, community-based organizations, and other partners throughout South Carolina and the Southeast. The University has been designated by the Carnegie Foundation as a “doctoral institution with highest research activity” and a “community-engaged institution.”The Department offers two undergraduate minors, including one in Nutrition and Food Systems, master’s programs including an MPH and online professional MPH, a doctoral PhD program, and graduate certificates in aging, global health, and health communication. Department faculty also contribute to teaching in the Arnold School’s undergraduate degree programs.USC is located in Columbia, South Carolina, a vibrant capital city offering abundant cultural, educational, and recreational opportunities. Columbia enjoys more than 300 days of sunshine annually and provides ready access to beaches, lakes, rivers, and mountains. The city hosts historical and cultural attractions, festivals, performing arts and sporting events, parks, and outdoor recreation, including Congaree National Park and 50,000-acre Lake Murray.
Required Education and Experience:
Applicants should have a doctoral degree in public health, nutrition, behavioral or social science, health services research, implementation science, or a closely related field by the start date of employment.
For the rank of Assistant Professor, applicants must demonstrate strong potential for scholarly productivity, excellence in teaching and mentoring, and success in establishing an externally funded research program.
Applicants for the rank of Associate Professor must have a strong record of funded research and scholarship, along with at least five years of experience as an effective instructor, mentor, and researcher by the start date of employment.

About the Department:
The Division of Academic & Student Affairs (DASA) is where students discover connections and community. It is where students live, where they gather, where they improve themselves, each other, and their university. DASA is where students seek guidance and support, both in and outside of the classroom. The division serves all students at NC State.
NC State wants employees to achieve their highest potential at work, learn more about our employee value proposition here (You Belong Here). The Division of Academic and Student Affairs is the place to work for values-driven faculty and staff who are passionate about promoting the success of the whole student.
The Department of Performing Arts and Technology offers a variety of technique, ensemble, and lecture courses. The Department has a growing major in Music Technology and also provides academic minors in Dance Studies, Dance Performance and Choreography, Music Studies, Music Performance, and Arts Entrepreneurship. The department has a full complement of course offerings, musical ensembles, and dance companies with a national reputation that attracts students from across the campus. More information about the department can be found at https://performingartstech.dasa.ncsu.edu/
Over the next year, the Department of Performing Arts and Technology will transition from the Division of Academic and Student Affairs (DASA) to the College of Humanities and Social Sciences (CHASS). The transition will create new opportunities for collaboration and closer connections with related disciplines while providing an academic structure that supports the department’s continued growth and success. Candidates joining the department will be part of this exciting transition and contribute to the department’s continued development within CHASS.
The Bachelor of Science in Music Technology is an interdisciplinary degree between Music and Technology degrees (e.g., Electrical and Computer Engineering). Students gain musical training through a musicianship core, applied musical instrument study, and a musical ensemble study. In parallel, students receive technical training through their core Math, Science, and technical concentration courses. Lastly, students combine these two through practical Music Technology courses that train students on the technical concepts for music and audio. Students receive training in the fundamentals of Acoustics, Psychoacoustics, Analog & Digital Audio technology, Musical Technology design, and algorithms. The plan concludes with the students fulfilling their core requirements, a senior design capstone project, and a music recital that has a technology component.
This plan will prepare students for a career designing and building electronic musical instruments, professional audio devices, sound systems for consumer devices, and software for music production and consumption.

The Department of Entomology and Plant Pathology invites applications for a nine-month, tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Insect Ecology with 60% effort in teaching and mentoring and 40% effort in research and discovery. We seek a dynamic scholar committed to excellence in undergraduate and graduate education, student engagement, and innovative teaching, alongside development of an active, externally funded research program.
The Assistant Professor will play a central role in the department’s undergraduate curriculum, including instruction of ENT 201: Insects and People, a high-enrollment course serving approximately 140 students in an in-person spring section and virtual sections offered in spring and fall. Additionally this role will contribute to additional undergraduate and graduate courses aligned with the faculty member’s expertise and departmental needs.
In addition to teaching, you will have the opportunity to establish a nationally recognized research program broadly focused on insect ecology, with research spanning areas such as insect behavior, plant–insect interactions, community ecology, conservation, global change biology, or related fields. Your research program will attract competitive extramural support from federal agencies, foundations, industry, and other sources while providing meaningful research and professional-development opportunities for undergraduate, graduate, and postdoctoral students.

Mentor undergraduate, M.S., and Ph.D. students through research, experiential learning, and career development.
Support student recruitment, retention, and success while contributing to departmental teaching initiatives.
Research and Discovery:
Develop and sustain an externally funded research program in insect ecology that complements and strengthens departmental expertise.
Conduct impactful research that may integrate field-based ecological studies with molecular, computational, spatial, or other data-driven approaches, and maintain a strong record of peer-reviewed publications and scholarly productivity.
Engage undergraduate and graduate students in research, providing meaningful training and mentorship.
Collaborate with departmental, university, and external partners to advance research, teaching, and outreach goals.

Job Details
The School of Music at Boston University’s College of Fine Arts seeks to hire an experienced collaborative piano teacher and performer as an associate professor. An appointment is sought to begin July 1, 2027.
This position requires excellent applied teaching skills and a professional performance profile of national recognition. The successful candidate will lead an established collaborative piano degree program in the areas of instrumental and vocal music; teach lessons, mentor and advise MM and DMA collaborative piano students; oversee all collaborative piano curricula; organize graduate assistant collaborative partnership assignments; coach chamber ensembles; and teach courses in sonata repertoire and vocal coaching.
Key Job Responsibilities:
Recruit and teach a studio of graduate students in collaborative piano Teach courses in vocal coaching and collaborative repertoire, vocal and instrumental Serve as academic advisor to all collaborative piano majors Facilitate collaborative piano assignments with faculty and students across all ensemble and applied areas of the School Maintain a national performance profile
The candidate will have a record of successful teaching at the collegiate-conservatory level, a nationally recognized performance profile, and the ability to recruit high-level collaborative piano majors at the MM and DMA levels. jobs.description:
Job Details
Valparaiso University invites applications for the position of Assistant Professor of Civil Engineering (https://www.valpo.edu/college-of-engineering/). Valparaiso University (“Valpo”), a community of learning grounded in the Lutheran tradition of scholarship, freedom, and faith, prepares students to lead and serve both church and society. Located one hour southeast of Chicago on a 310-acre campus, Valpo is a comprehensive university with an enrollment of approximately 2,100 undergraduate and graduate students. Valpo is consistently recognized as one of the best private universities in the Midwest and has an increasingly diverse student body.
Valparaiso University’s undergraduate-only College of Engineering offers ABET-accredited degrees in Civil Engineering. The College of Engineering at Valpo is currently ranked in the top 10% of Engineering Programs (non-doctoral) in the 2026 U.S. News and World Report rankings.
Qualifications
The successful candidate will be responsible for teaching undergraduate courses, developing a research program that incorporates undergraduate students, and providing service to the department and profession. Teaching responsibilities could include courses in structural engineering, introductory civil engineering courses, the civil engineering capstone design sequence, and general engineering courses.
Candidates should have a strong commitment to teaching excellence and have the ability to communicate effectively with students and colleagues. The candidate shall have the legal authority to work in the USA, shall have completed a Ph.D. in civil engineering or a closely related discipline, and will have obtained their professional engineering license prior to the conclusion of the tenure track period. Additionally, preference will be given to candidates with previous teaching experience.
Candidates should have a Ph.D. (ABD considered) by August 2027 in Civil Engineering with a focus on Structural Engineering, or a closely related field.
Application Instructions
As a campus with an increasingly diverse student body, we encourage applications from individuals with commitment and experience in mentoring students from an array of backgrounds.
Please submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae, teaching statement, research statement, and contact information for three references to Interfolio at https://apply.interfolio.com/193924. In your cover letter, please include brief statements of (a) how you might contribute to the university’s distinctive mission, and (b) what experiences you have had which will enable you to mentor a diverse student body. Candidates who submit names of references should expect that the search committee will contact these references in confidence and that credentials will be confirmed prior to hire. Candidates should also expect that the search committee will review their LinkedIn profile. Employment will require a satisfactory criminal background check.
Applications will be accepted until the position is filled; however, the committee will begin reviewing applications on November 16, 2026.
About the Community:
Valpo is located in Valparaiso Indiana, a county seat of 35,000 residents with high quality schools and an active social community located 50 miles from downtown Chicago and only 14 miles from the beautiful Indiana Dunes National Park. Valparaiso is home to 13 city parks, over 20 miles of bike trails, and award-winning downtown gathering spaces that house year-round community events including: the Popcorn Festival, music concerts, ice skating, farmer’s markets and more. The city was built to support neighborhood activities, with most neighborhoods being within walking distance of parks, schools, and communal spaces. With the university located less than one mile from downtown, its central location within the community makes it easy for employees to enjoy the growing amenities the city has to offer. Valparaiso has been recognized as one of the top communities in Indiana and is in one of the fastest growing counties in the state. It is an area that continues to show economic growth and diversification of its residents.

About Us
For more than 60 years, Kennesaw State University has been known for its entrepreneurial spirit and sense of community. A leader in innovative teaching and learning, Kennesaw State is located just north of Atlanta and combines a suburban setting on two metro-Atlanta campuses in Kennesaw and Marietta. As one of Georgia's largest universities, Kennesaw State offers undergraduate and graduate degrees to over 50,000 students. Our high-impact research and Division I athletics also draw students from throughout the region and across the globe. A member of the University System of Georgia, Kennesaw State is a Carnegie-designated doctoral research institution (R2) committed to becoming a world-class academic institution positioned to broaden its academic and research missions and expand its scope on a local, regional, and national level.
Our university's vibrant culture, career opportunities, rich benefits, and values of respect, integrity, collaboration, inclusivity, and accountability make us an employer of choice. As part of the University System of Georgia, Kennesaw State exemplifies the power and promise of a student-centered, research-driven university. In addition, Kennesaw State supports the University of Georgia's core values of accountability, excellence, integrity, and respect. We are searching for talented people to join Kennesaw State University in our vision. For more information, visit the Kennesaw State University website.
Location
Our Kennesaw campus is located at 1000 Chastain Road NW, Kennesaw, GA 30144. Our Marietta campus is located at 1100 South Marietta Parkway, Marietta, GA 30060.
Department Information
The Department of Psychological Science is a large and dynamic department in the Norman J. Radow College of Humanities and Social Sciences. The Department has more than 50 full-time and many part-time faculty supporting a major and minor in psychology, including a fully online undergraduate program. In the Department of Psychological Science, our accomplished faculty guide students in the study of behavior and mental processes through a comprehensive program that promotes scientific thinking and cultivates transferable skills that lead to meaningful careers. Our psychology majors gain valuable hands-on experiences and skill-building opportunities across the curriculum by engaging in high-impact practices such as study abroad programs, internships, peer mentoring, and research experiences. Committed to rigorous scholarly activity and evidence-based teaching, we develop students as global citizens, competent interns, peer educators, skilled researchers, and confident leaders who are well-prepared for the next stages of their personal and professional journeys. The Department promotes respect, integrity, collaboration, inclusivity, and accountability in all aspects of work. We seek candidates whose endeavors exemplify the values of Kennesaw State University and whose experiences have prepared them to fulfill our department's commitment to the success of our students, faculty, staff, and communities.
With more than 400 full-time faculty and 8,100 degree-seeking students, the Norman J. Radow College of Humanities & Social Sciences is dedicated to pioneering workforce readiness in the humanities and social sciences. By staying true to our Liberal Arts values and integrating practical knowledge and experiential learning into our curriculum, we empower our students to become responsible citizens ready for the demands of the modern workplace. The home of three schools and eight departments, the College offers more than 80 graduate and undergraduate programs of study in both traditional and interdisciplinary fields. These programs enable students to develop leadership, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills, as well as a strong sense of civic engagement.
The College is committed to the success of our students, faculty, staff and communities. We seek candidates whose experience has prepared them to fulfill that commitment and engage our students, partners, and stakeholders effectively.
Job Summary
Kennesaw State University is now accepting applications for a full-time, tenure track faculty position as Assistant Professor of Psychology (Physiological/Biological Psychology or Behavioral/Cognitive Neuroscience) in the Department of Psychological Science with a preferred start date of August 2027. This is a nine-month contracted position and is for work to be performed in the state of Georgia.
Responsibilities
Develop and maintain a productive program of research in physiological/biological psychology or behavioral/cognitive neuroscience.
Publish scholarly work in peer-reviewed journals and disseminate research findings through professional presentations and other scholarly outlets.
Seek external funding to support research and scholarly activity.
Teach undergraduate courses in the candidate's area of specialization and courses that are part of the Psychology curriculum (e.g., Physiological Psychology, Perception, Advanced Laboratory in Psychological Science, Psychopharmacology).
Teach courses of varying modalities and sizes, including large class sizes, on the Kennesaw and/or Marietta campuses. The standard teaching load is 9 credit hours (i.e., 3 courses) per semester; however, workload distributions are negotiable.
Engage students in research and provide mentorship that supports their academic and professional development.
Contribute to departmental, college, and university service activities, including committee work and shared governance.
Engage in professional activities relevant to the candidate's area of expertise.
Teaching assignments will be based on earned degrees and SACSCOC Faculty Credentials Guidelines.
Required Qualifications
An earned Doctorate degree, or the foreign equivalent, in Psychology or a closely related discipline is required at the time of hire.
Demonstrated record of research and scholarship within the discipline.
Experience teaching, mentoring, and/or supporting student success in higher education settings
Preferred Qualifications
Specialization in physiological/biological psychology or behavioral/cognitive neuroscience.
A record of publishing scholarship in reputable outlets.
Experience/potential in securing external funding.
Experience teaching courses related to physiological/biological psychology or behavioral/cognitive neuroscience, as well as courses that are part of the Psychology curriculum (e.g., Physiological Psychology, Perception, Advanced Laboratory in Psychological Science, Psychopharmacology).
Evidence of effectiveness in teaching in different modalities (i.e., face-to-face, online, hybrid).
Effectiveness in supervision and mentoring of students.
Required Documents to Attach
CV

feedback from presentations, workshops, etc.) - Upload as Additional Documents

Apply Before Date

Location: Philadelphia, PA

Children's Hospital of Philadelphia and the Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine at the Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania seek candidates for an Assistant Professor position in the non-tenure clinician educator track. Expertise is required in the specific area of clinical immunology and flow cytometry. A strong preference will be given to applicants with experience in innovation and clinical assay development. Applicants must have an M.D. and/or Ph.D degree. MD applicants must be board certified in Clinical Pathology (AP/CP or CP) and eligible for medical licensure in Pennsylvania. jobs.title: Faculty, Substance Abuse Counseling and Psychology
jobs.description:
Job Details
SUMMARY STATEMENT
This full-time, tenure-track faculty position is responsible for providing high-quality, accessible instruction and supporting student success through excellence in teaching, professional development, scholarship, and service. Faculty members are expected to contribute to the mission and strategic goals of Hagerstown Community College (HCC) through instruction, assessment, curriculum development, student mentorship, shared governance, and community engagement. As exempt employees, faculty have an expected work week of 37.5 hours and maintain a significant campus presence during the 10-month contract period.
The faculty member serves within the Behavioral and Social Science and contributes to the ongoing development, assessment, and continuous improvement of the Substance Abuse Counseling concentration. The position includes responsibilities related to student learning outcomes assessment, curriculum development, adjunct faculty support, and institutional service.
ORGANIZATIONAL RELATIONSHIPS
A. Faculty reports directly to the Division Director of the Behavioral and Social Science.
B. Faculty collaborates with the Division Director, Behavioral and Social Science faculty, other division colleagues, student support personnel, and other college stakeholders.
FACULTY ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES
A. TEACHING –A faculty member is expected to prepare for and teach an assigned instructional load (15 credits in the fall and spring terms) with a minimum of 5 office hours per week. As part of their teaching duties, faculty are expected to:
1. Utilize effective instructional activities and strategies that support learning outcomes and promote effective engagement for student learning and achievement.
2. Develop methods of assessment that align with the learning outcomes at the course, program, general education, and institutional levels.
3. Utilize assessment results to support continuous improvement of instruction, curriculum, and student success initiatives to submit outcome assessment reports by the required deadlines.
4. Contribute to the continuous review, development, and improvement of curriculum. Faculty are expected to incorporate current disciplinary knowledge, emerging technologies, and evidence-based instructional practices into course content and delivery.
5. Maintain current course materials in the appropriate learning management repository and updating as needed to align with college expectations and all legal requirements (i.e. federal accessibility, etc.).
6. Provide clear effective communication by maintaining accessibility and regular, substantive interaction with students to ensure expectations are clearly conveyed and adequate feedback is provided on academic work.
7. Advocate and mentor students by fostering an inclusive learning environment, providing guidance and support as appropriate. Advise students regarding academic progress, program requirements, transfer opportunities, and career pathways by collaborating with appropriate college personnel (Advising, Learning Support Services, Career Services, Workforce Development, etc.).
8. Maintain accurate records of attendance and scholastic performance and submit all requirements (i.e. financial aid attendance, midterm/final grades, etc.) by required deadlines.
B. SCHOLARSHIP AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT - A faculty member engages in ongoing professional development to maintain disciplinary expertise, enhance instructional effectiveness, support scholarship, and contribute to institutional priorities. Examples include but are not limited to:
1. Attending required New Faculty onboarding and training (i.e. New Faculty Orientation/Group Meetings, D2L/Technology training, Quality Matters, Teaching in the Community College).
2. Attending conferences, seminars or workshops that have received prior approval from appropriate administrative areas.
3. Creating professional works or publications (i.e. articles, books, art or music performances, etc.).
4. Completing relevant graduate coursework or other professional trainings, internships, practical field work, etc.
5. Other projects such as reviewing or editing publications, participating in professional organization discussions or peer partnerships projects.
C. SERVICE – the extent to which a faculty member provides college or community service is factored into promotion criteria and should align with the strategic goals and mission of the college. Examples include but are not limited to:
1. Participation through service on departmental, divisional, and institutional committees (i.e. search committee, program review, accreditation, ad hoc or other shared governance groups.
2. Provide guidance and support to adjunct faculty to promote consistency in curriculum implementation, assessment practices, instructional quality, and student learning outcomes in alignment with the College's mission and goals.
3. Contribute to promotion of the College’s mission and strategic plan through the provision of time or expertise/advisement for programming, initiative development and student-oriented activities for outreach, enrollment and retention (i.e. Unit Planning, grants, Open House/Career Fair events, etc.),
4. Serves as an ambassador for the College and their discipline by participating in activities that support and sustain partnerships between the college, community and external groups to promote community engagement or outreach.
FACULTY PROGRAM SPECIFIC RESPONSIBLITIES
D. Supervise required internships
E. Chair the program’s Advisory Committee
F. Seek out and maintain close relationships with local agencies that work with Substance Abuse clients
EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCEA Masters degree is required within the appropriate discipline. SKILLS AND ABILITIESPreference will be given to candidates with recent teaching experience at the undergraduate or community college level. Candidates must possess strong organizational, advising, and interpersonal skills, with a demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with students, faculty, staff, and administrators. Strong instructional and classroom management skills are required. WORKING ENVIRONMENT Some evening classes may be required.

Candidates with backgrounds in software engineering or web development are of interest for at least one position, though all interested candidates with strong general computer science backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

Conduct scholarly activities (e.g., research) in the field of specialization.
Active engagement in student-centered activities (e.g., research) in the field of specialization.

Job Details
Assistant Professor of English: Global/Postcolonial Englishes
Overview: Illinois Wesleyan University invites applications for the position of Assistant Professor of English (Tenure Track). The start date for this position is August 15, 2027.
Qualifications: We seek a scholar-teacher whose work in global/postcolonial Englishes explores class, gender, race, ethnicity, migration/diaspora, and/or queer/trans identities, optimally in ways that are in conversation with British literature(s) of the eighteenth and/or nineteenth centuries. Candidates must have a Ph.D. in English, Comparative Literature, or another closely related field by August 15, 2027. They must be dedicated to undergraduate education, enthusiastic about professional engagement with students in and out of the classroom, and able to work in teams in a collegial environment.
About the Tenure Track: At Illinois Wesleyan, Tenure Track faculty engage students through six teaching assignments each year, produce scholarly work, serve as academic advisors, and engage in departmental and campus-wide service. After receiving feedback on formative reviews in the second, third, and fourth years of employment, a case for tenure and promotion is submitted in the fall of the sixth year.
Tenure track faculty are eligible for sabbatical following six complete academic years of full-time service and every seven years thereafter. Additional professional development opportunities currently include start-up funds, pre-tenure faculty leave, and support for the development of external grants. The Thorpe Center for Curricular and Faculty Development supports faculty in their teaching and scholarly and/or artistic work, including peer-to-peer mentoring, workshops, internal grants, and assistance with instructional design and technology.
About IWU: Founded in 1850, Illinois Wesleyan University is a nationally ranked, small, private, undergraduate liberal arts university with highly selective admission criteria and a tradition of teaching excellence emphasizing the integration of the liberal arts and professional education. We are located in Bloomington, Illinois, a metro area of 190,000 people, which is about a two or three hour drive from Chicago, St. Louis, and Indianapolis. We are strongly committed to fostering an environment that values varied perspectives and backgrounds.
Responsibilities of Tenure-Track Faculty:
6-course teaching load per year
Academic advising in the discipline
Scholarly and/or artistic achievement
Departmental and University service
Application Information: Please submit the following as separate .pdf attachments and/or via Interfolio to english@iwu.edu:
a cover letter addressing qualifications, including scholarly achievement and plans for future scholarly work; teaching philosophy, experience, and aspirations; and service to relevant disciplines, institutions, and/or communities;
a curriculum vitae
a statement that:
addresses how your philosophy and practice have contributed to fostering an environment that values varied perspectives and backgrounds and
notes how you would collaborate at IWU to embrace a wide range of experiences and viewpoints.
Review of applications will begin on October 12 and will continue until the position has been filled. Candidates selected for further stages of the search will be asked to submit additional materials, which may include three letters of recommendation, a writing sample, teaching materials, and unofficial transcripts.
Questions may be directed to: Brandi Reissenweber, English Department Chair, breissen@iwu.edu
Compensation and Benefits:
Nine-month appointment

jobs.title: Assistant Professor in Mental Health Counseling
jobs.description:
Job ID: 7535
Job Summary
Central Washington University is recruiting an Assistant Professor in Mental Health Counseling to join our Psychology team in Ellensburg, Washington. This role is an important member of our team as they enhance the vision for the University. The role is a campus-based position, which means you get to see the lives you are impacting. We're offering a competitive salary plus the awesome CWU benefits.
Who we are:
We are a team of individuals committed to Changing Students' Lives. No matter what job, each of us plays a part in supporting and empowering our students to fulfill their dreams.
Working in higher education provides career growth and career choice. Think of a university campus like a mini city, operating across 380 acres. You'll find robust academics, libraries, athletics and sporting events, full service and quick serve dining, conferences and events from small to large, recreation centers, housing, health services, police and public safety for the campus population of ~8,300 students.
Central Washington University has been named a Fulbright U.S. Scholar Program Top Producing Institution for the 2022-2023 academic year. In addition, for seven out of eight years, CWU was a recipient of the prestigious Higher Education Excellence in Diversity (HEED) Award from INSIGHT Into Diversity magazine. RentCafe has also named CWU #13 of the Top 20 Best College Towns in the U.S. in 2025.
Come join us on our journey to encourage, inspire, and create spaces where all identities thrive on campus.
Tour our campus in Ellensburg here. www.youtube.com/watch?v=HjdhOegDa9A
What we offer:
Our investment in you begins the day you join our team, a healthy and successful future for you is important to us. We offer medical, dental, life and disability insurance, retirement and optional savings plans, tuition assistance for you and your dependents, discounts across town, an employee assistance program for individualized counseling, and a wellness incentive program. Learn more: Benefits, Perks, and Leave and Total Rewards Calculator.
The Role:
The Department of Psychology at Central Washington University (Ellensburg, WA) seeks an Assistant Professor for a tenure-track position, specifically to support the reestablishment of the Mental Health Counseling master's program, which was relaunched in 2025. Candidates should exhibit a commitment to teaching, developing their individual scholarship, involving students in research, advising graduate students, and mentoring undergraduate psychology students. Candidates should be prepared to teach graduate-level counseling and undergraduate-level psychology and/or behavioral health courses, be eligible to supervise counseling practica and/or internship, and provide quality service to the department, university, community, and their profession.
This position is initially funded by a generous donation from Comprehensive Healthcare, a regional behavioral health services organization, after which it will be assumed by the university.
At CWU, we pride ourselves in upholding our mission and vision to create transformative educational environments that encourage personal growth and success. Faculty will integrate Central Washington University's vision which is "CWU will be a model learning community of access and opportunity". In order to build a community of access and opportunity, Central Washington University nurtures culturally sustaining practices that expand access and success to all students. We are committed to fostering high impact practices, sustainability, and authentic community partnerships that are grounded in meaningful relationships.
This position is an in-person position on the Ellensburg campus. The faculty member who accepts this position must be willing to commit to teaching on the Ellensburg campus and have the desire and skills to effectively teach in-person and online or in web enhanced courses via both synchronous and asynchronous formats.
Minimum Qualifications
Please address in your cover letter:
Meet one of the following education requirements by September 16, 2027:
Have an earned doctoral degree in counselor education, preferably from a CACREP accredited program;
OR have a related doctoral degree and have been employed as a full-time faculty member in a counselor education program for a minimum of one full academic year before July 1, 2013;
OR have been employed as a full-time doctoral-level faculty member in a CORE-accredited master's program prior to July 1, 2017;
OR have graduated from a rehabilitation doctoral program prior to January 1, 2018.
License eligible as a counselor in the state of Washington.
Professional identity as a counselor educator, including participation in professional activities, scholarly activities, and/or service to the profession.
Preferred Qualifications (Please address in your cover letter):
Demonstrated commitment and/or experience to mentoring students in undergraduate and/or graduate research and through teaching and/or mentoring activities.
Experience as a licensed clinician in the field of counseling.
Experience with teaching graduate and/or undergraduate level psychology courses that can engage and inspire students from a variety of identities and backgrounds.
Record of scholarly productivity.
Familiarity with CACREP requirements and the willingness to support the Program Coordinator in meeting all accreditation reporting requirements.
Training and experience in the provision of distance-based education and clinical services.
Research, teaching, and service that demonstrate an ability to contribute to Central's vision to create a model learning community of access and opportunity.
Competencies

Adaptability/Flexibility: Responds positively to changing program needs and responsibilities. Adapts approach and methods to achieve results; recovers quickly from setbacks and finds alternatives.
Commitment to Belonging: Values the uniqueness of every individual and fosters an environment where everyone feels respected and empowered to thrive.

jobs.title: Open Rank Tenure-line Faculty in Computer Science
jobs.description:
Job Details
Description
The Department of Computer Science at the University of Virginia (UVA) invites applications for multiple tenured or tenure-track faculty positions at all ranks.
We seek outstanding researchers and educators who will contribute to the continued growth, excellence, and intellectual breadth of the Department. The Department has substantial research strengths spanning artificial intelligence and machine learning, computer systems, architecture, cyber-physical systems, human-centered computing, robotics and autonomous systems, security, privacy, and cryptography, software engineering and programming languages, and algorithms and theory. We are particularly interested in candidates who will enhance and connect with the university’s AI research initiatives in both foundational and applied AI research, but also welcome applications across the full spectrum of computer science, including foundational research, emerging areas of computing, interdisciplinary research, and work that creates connections across established fields.
The primary responsibilities for these tenured/tenure-track positions include developing an internationally recognized research program, teaching and mentoring, and service to the department, university, public, and professional community. The appointment rank will be commensurate with experience and qualifications.
Our department is proud of its strong culture of collaboration and collegiality and is committed to sustaining and strengthening it. Faculty collaborate extensively throughout the School of Engineering and Applied Science and with colleagues in UVA’s Schools of Data Science, Medicine, Nursing, Law, Public Policy, Business, Education, and Arts & Sciences. These connections foster opportunities for foundational and interdisciplinary research spanning computing, science, engineering, health, and society.
Computer Science plays a key role in several major interdisciplinary research efforts at UVA. The Department is a founding member of the Link Lab, a multidisciplinary research center bringing together researchers in computer science, electrical and computer engineering, mechanical and aerospace engineering, and systems engineering to advance cyber-physical systems, robotics, autonomous systems, and the Internet of Things. CS faculty are also deeply engaged with UVA’s Biocomplexity Institute, university-wide efforts in artificial intelligence and data science, and interdisciplinary initiatives spanning health, biotechnology, neuroscience, and digital technology and society.
UVA is making substantial investments in computing and artificial intelligence research, including state-of-the-art high-performance computing and GPU infrastructure for large-scale AI, machine learning, data analytics, and computational science, and university-wide AI initiatives for researchers at all stages. These investments complement a growing university-wide community working on both the foundations of AI and its applications across science, engineering, health, and society.
The Department offers Ph.D. and master’s degrees through the School of Engineering and Applied Science and bachelor’s degrees through both the School of Engineering and Applied Science and the College of Arts & Sciences. Computer Science also collaborates with the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering to jointly administer UVA’s undergraduate and graduate Computer Engineering programs.
UVA is a highly selective undergraduate and graduate institution and one of the nation’s leading public universities. UVA is situated in the beautiful city of Charlottesville, Virginia, a picturesque and vibrant small city consistently recognized as one of the nation's top places to reside. UVA's location offers proximity to Washington D.C., enriching opportunities for collaboration and engagement with numerous federal organizations. More information about the city, the school, faculty benefits and other topics can be found at https://hr.virginia.edu/careers-uva/why-uva.
In conjunction with these positions, senior graduate students are eligible and encouraged to consider the UVA Engineering Rising Scholars program. This program is designed to encourage early-career scholars to pursue a career in academia by supporting their postdoctoral work before beginning a tenure-track position at the University of Virginia. Detailed information and application instructions are available at https://engineering.virginia.edu/rising-scholars-postdoctoral-program
Qualifiations
Candidates must have received a doctorate or equivalent in a computing field by the start of their appointment. Evidence of a commitment to high-impact scholarship, funded research, undergraduate- and graduate-level teaching and advising excellence, professional and university service, and mentoring are expected.
Application Instructions
Applications should be submitted via Interfolio. Review of applications will begin on November 15, 2026. The application package must include:
a cover letter
a curriculum vitae
research statement
teaching philosophy statement
service statement
three representative research papers;
In addition, the names and contact information of at least three individuals that can serve as references should be provided.
The University will perform background checks on all new faculty hires prior to making a final offer of employment.
For questions about these positions, please contact Ferdinando Fioretto, Associate Professor, at fioretto@virginia.edu.

jobs.title: Open Rank Tenure-ineligible Faculty in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Details
Description
The School of Engineering and Applied Science (SEAS) at the University of Virginia (UVA) seeks candidates for an Academic General Faculty (AGF) position specializing in laboratory instruction, and injury biomechanics and trauma prevention research, for the Center for Applied Biomechanics (CAB) and the Department of Mechanical & Aerospace Engineering (MAE).
The primary responsibilities for this tenure-ineligible position include teaching mechanical engineering courses with a particular focus on hands-on, laboratory-based undergraduate courses; research; and service to the department, university and professional community. The appointment rank will be commensurate with experience and qualifications. Compensation is contingent upon experience. This period of appointment will be for 3 years contingent on the availability of research funding, with the possibility of renewal.
The teaching duties include (but are not limited to) leading multiple core undergraduate laboratory courses in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering. A core part of our curriculum is a progression of hands-on, laboratory-based courses beginning with basic exercises in fundamental mechanics, and progressing to independent experimental design and analysis in team-based projects. The AGF Professor will aid in this critical part of our curriculum by leading one or more laboratory courses per semester.
The research duties include performing fundamental and applied research in injury biomechanics, trauma prevention, and public health and safety at the UVA Center for Applied Biomechanics. The AGF Professor will be expected to develop and maintain a dynamic research program, develop research funding (often in collaboration with other faculty), advise MS and PhD students, and collaborate with the Center’s other researchers in continuing to lead the field of injury biomechanics and trauma prevention with a focus on public health and safety.
The CAB is one of the largest university-based automobile safety and injury biomechanics research centers in the world. It was founded in 1989 and has grown steadily since. Currently the Center operates with a staff of approximately 50 researchers and support staff, including 8 Principal Investigators from SEAS and the School of Medicine, in a dedicated, state-of-the-art, 35,000 ft2 facility with world-class computational, experimental, mechanical, and biological resources. UVA and SEAS have made it a priority to encourage interdisciplinary research, and the AGF Professor will strategically position the Center's trauma prevention and public health research programs and enhance CAB’s reputation as a world-leader in the field. This position will also benefit from new opportunities in Engineering, Health and Cyber-Physical Systems across grounds to provide transformational investments in the quality of UVA's research.
This position is based in Charlottesville at our principal location. UVA is a highly selective undergraduate and graduate institution that annually ranks as one of the premiere public universities in the United States, with one of the highest graduation rates in the nation. UVA is situated in Charlottesville, Virginia, a picturesque and vibrant small city consistently recognized as one of the nation's top places to reside. UVA's location offers proximity to Washington D.C., enriching opportunities for collaboration and engagement with numerous federal organizations. More information about the city, the school, faculty benefits and other topics can be found at https://hr.virginia.edu/careers-uva/why-uva.
Qualifiations
Candidates must possess a PhD in Mechanical Engineering, or a closely related field, and have experience in injury biomechanics and trauma prevention research with a focus on public health and safety, in areas such as
epidemiological studies to elucidate injury risk factors and variations in the population
statistical analyses of large field-data and experimental-based datasets\
the biomechanics of injury prediction and mitigation
laboratory impact experimentation with various biological and non-biological human surrogate models
In addition, candidates must have experience mentoring students in a laboratory setting, in areas such as
laboratory safety and good lab practices
project management
reporting and technical communication
student-led independent research
The candidates who have a proven record of project management, team building, and service-oriented leadership are preferred. Preference will also be given to candidates who have a demonstrated record of collaborative relationships across departments, with other universities, and with medical school researchers.
Application Instructions
Apply for this position in Interfolio . Provide the following in PDF format:
Cover letter that summarizes your areas of research/scholarship, mentorship, and areas of potential collaboration at the University of Virigina. To help us organize our review of applications, please also specifically list your primary areas of research in boldface at the top of your letter;
Curriculum vitae (including research, teaching/mentorship, service, and leadership experience);
A statement describing your current research, future directions and broader impacts;
A statement describing your teaching philosophy, including your anticipated approach to hands-on, laboratory-based instruction
A statement describing demonstrated contributions to fostering inclusive practices that create climates in which all stakeholders can achieve their maximum potential (please focus on skills and experience, not beliefs and opinions);
A single file that includes two research papers that best represent your work.
You will also request 3-5 references directly in Interfolio by providing names and contact information in the application. These reference requests will be generated immediately once you submit your application.
Review of applications will begin on October 19, 2026 and will continue until the position is filled. The University will perform background checks on all new faculty hires prior to making a final offer of employment.
For questions about this position, please contact Jason Forman, Search Committee Chair, at jlf3m@virginia.edu.

jobs.title: Open Rank Tenure Track Faculty in English Education
jobs.description:
Position
The Department of Teaching and Learning in the College of Education at the University of Iowa invites applications for one 9-month academic-year tenure-track faculty position at the rank of assistant, associate, or full professor in the English Education program. The position will begin August 18, 2027.
Description
We seek an individual with evidence of significant professional promise or accomplishment in research that impacts English Education. The successful applicant will be expected to maintain a robust program of scholarship, teach undergraduate and graduate courses in English Education, and advise MA students in English Education and PhD students in the Language, Literacy, and Social Studies Education (LLSSE) program. We seek applicants who actively engage with faculty, staff, students, and the community to foster education that prioritizes access, opportunity, and belonging for all those involved in the growth and development of students.
Responsibilities
Major responsibilities include: conducting an active program of research and building a scholarly research agenda in education; designing and teaching undergraduate/graduate courses in teacher education in the Department of Teaching and Learning; and advising both English Education MA students and PhD students in the Language, Literacy, and Social Studies Education (LLSSE). In addition, the successful candidate will be expected to pursue and secure external funding; contribute to national and international scholarship; be involved with local, state, and national activities that support the practice of English Education; and participate in service to the program, department, college, and university. Faculty are required to engage in at least 4 hours per semester of collaboration with teachers in contributing to instruction in K12 classrooms.
Education Requirement
Prospective candidates must have earned a doctorate in English Education or a related discipline by August 1, 2027.
Required Qualifications
(1) Evidence of scholarly productivity or promise of scholarly productivity (rank dependent)
(2) Experience in English Education instruction
(3) Demonstrated knowledge of, and application of, effective strategies for working with faculty, staff, and students from a variety of backgrounds and perspectives
(4) Teaching expertise in at least one or more of the following areas of interest within secondary English/Literacy Education: writing pedagogy, young adult literature, secondary reading, language variation, critical literacy, culturally responsive/sustaining pedagogy, social justice, multilingualism, media literacy, multimodal literacies, drama and performance, classroom discourse and teacher education
Desirable Qualifications
(1) Successful experience teaching in K-12 settings
(2) Evidence of excellent teaching skills at the undergraduate and graduate level
(3) Licensure (or eligibility for licensure) in English/Literacy Education at the secondary level
(4) A record of securing external funds for research, training, and program development
(5) Interest in building partnerships across campus and with local schools and communities
Salary
Competitive and commensurate with qualifications and experience. Excellent start-up package, benefits and research support.
Location
Onsite in Iowa City, Iowa
Application Materials
To apply, please submit the following materials:
Cover Letter addressing all qualifications noted above
Curriculum Vitae
Sample of scholarly writing
Graduate college transcripts
Contact information for three references
To apply for this position, go to our website at https://jobs.uiowa.edu/jobSearch/faculty/ and choose requisition number 76043.
Screening
Review of applications will begin in October 2026 and continue until the position is filled.
Inquiries
Direct general questions about the position to Dr. Charlotte Land (charlotte-land@uiowa.edu) and/or Dr. Pam Wesely pamela-wesely@uiowa.edu, and questions about the application procedure to Rachel Wallace (rachel-wallace@uiowa.edu), Faculty Affairs Manager.
Additional Information
Successful candidates will be required to self-disclose any misconduct history or pending research misconduct investigation, including but not limited to sexual misconduct in prior employment, and provide a related release. Final candidates will be subject to a criminal background and credential check.
If your H-1B petition is subject to the September 19, 2025, Presidential Proclamation, please note that the department will NOT cover the $100,000 payment associated with H-1B sponsorship, either at the time of hire or for international travel purposes. We encourage you to explore alternative pathways for work authorization. Our team is available to help identify options that may be suitable for your situation.
Persons with disabilities who need assistance or accommodations with the application or interview process may contact University Human Resources/Faculty and Staff Disability Services at (319) 335-2660 or fsds@uiowa.edu.
The University of Iowa is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration for employment free from discrimination on the basis of race, creed, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, pregnancy (including childbirth and related conditions), disability, genetic information, status as a U.S. veteran, service in the U.S. military, sexual orientation, or associational preferences.
Why Join Us?
At the University of Iowa, you’ll thrive in a collaborative, welcoming, and intellectually rich environment. As a Big Ten, R1 institution, we offer the resources of a major university with the personal connections of a close-knit academic community. Our faculty are supported at every stage of their careers through mentorship, professional development, and leadership opportunities. Located in Iowa City, one of the most livable cities in America, you’ll enjoy a vibrant cultural scene, top-rated schools, and a welcoming community that values creativity, innovation, and work-life integration. Learn more about this community and resources at WorkLife at Iowa.
About the College
Recognized as the State of Iowa's top College of Education, we offer more than 80 undergraduate and graduate degree programs, including licensure, endorsement, and certificate programs, many of which are regularly ranked among the best in the nation. Students study with our world-renowned faculty who are the leaders in their fields. Our college is comprised of four departments: Educational Policy and Leadership Studies, Psychological and Quantitative Foundations, Counselor Education, and Teaching and Learning. The College houses several Centers that support work in critical areas of education, including UI REACH, Iowa Reading Research Center, Scanlan Center for School Mental Health, and the Belin-Blank Center for Gifted Education and Talent Development. The College is guided by a Strategic Plan which defines our mission and the vision and values that bolster it.
About the Department and English Education
The Department of Teaching and Learning (T & L) at the University of Iowa includes over 40 faculty members and 900 students. It includes undergraduate teacher education program areas as well as MAT/MS/MA and PhD graduate programs. The incoming scholar will contribute to undergraduate and MA programs in English Education as well as the Ph.D. program in Language, Literacy, and Social Studies Education (LLSSE). The English Education program features carefully designed practicum experiences in schools, where students have the opportunity to tutor, coach, and teach in classrooms. Students study literature, writing, drama, digital media, and other contemporary topics through classes taken from the world-renowned English department as well as coursework in pedagogy and literacy.
The LLSSE Ph.D. program brings together interdisciplinary scholarly traditions and contemporary theory in Literacy and Cultural Studies, Multilingual Education and Applied Linguistics, and Social Studies Education. The LCLE program provides students with the necessary content-area knowledge, interdisciplinary expertise, and research skills for independent research and varied leadership positions in LCLE Education.
