jobs.description:
FORT VALLEY STATE UNIVERSITY (FVSU), a state and land-grant institution of the University System of Georgia, invites applications for the position of Assistant Professor of Agricultural Engineering and Technology.
Fort Valley State University, the only 1890 land-grant university in Georgia, is a comprehensive institution that provides an education to over 2,800 students including graduate students. The university is located in the town of Fort Valley in Peach County, the original site of the state's peach industry. Its 1,365-acre (5.52 km2) campus is Georgia's second-largest public university in area.
Fort Valley State University is an affirmative action, equal opportunity institution and does not discriminate against applicants, students, or employees on the basis of race, gender, ethnicity, national origin, sexual orientation, religion, age, disability, or marital or veteran status.
JOB SUMMARY
The College of Agriculture, Family Sciences and Technology (CAFST) seeks an energetic and student-focused faculty member with expertise in Agricultural Engineering Technology (AET) for a 9-month, tenure-track Assistant Professor position. This is a dual appointment shared between the Departments of Agricultural Sciences (25% teaching) and Agricultural Research (75%).
The successful candidate will be responsible for teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in Agricultural Engineering Technology as determined by departmental needs. Specific teaching assignments will be made by the Department Chair.
The faculty member will also plan an important role in student advising and mentorship, including providing guidance and support to related student organizations. The successful candidate will assist in the recruitment of students into the Agricultural Engineering Technology program.
The position includes a strong research expectation. The successful candidate will be expected to develop a robust research program in discipline and collaborate with colleagues in the Cooperative Extension program.
MAJOR DUTIES
Provide high-quality instruction engineering courses and facilitate effective student learning in undergraduate and graduate courses in Agricultural Engineering Technology with a focus on machinery and instrumentation plus additional supporting core courses (e.g., programming, computer aided=drafting and design, thermodynamics, etc.) depending on the department's needs and candidate's expertise.
Engage with FVSU Research Farm personnel and industry partners, as needed, to successfully teach required course and complete research projects.
Design, prepare and supervise laboratory and experiential learning activities in discipline for students.
Use both internal (e.g. Desire to Learn (D2L)) and other instructional learning technologies to deliver course materials and engage students.
Develop course objectives, assignments, and effective methods for assisting student performance.
Modify existing courses or develop new courses, as needed, to create a dynamic curriculum that prepares students for professional careers.
Provide timely and constructive feedback on student work.
Engage undergraduate students in research and experiential learning opportunities.
Develop and maintain a robust, competitive research program as a platform for professional growth and student training, mentoring undergraduate research projects, and/or participation in professional organizations.
Secure extramural funding through competitive grants and collaborative partnerships.
Establish collaborations with appropriate industry partners to facilitate internships and other learning opportunities for students and help ensure relevancy of programs and curricula
Perform other job-related duties as assigned.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
Ph.D. in Agricultural Engineering, Agriculture and Biosystems Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or a closely related field.
Provide evidence of innovative instructional pedagogy including familiarity of AI integration in the discipline
Demonstrated industry and/or research expertise in the area(s) of machinery systems engineering, machine design, instrumentation or control system development.
Ability to teach undergraduate courses in introductory engineering, computer programming, computer aided drafting (CAD), off-road machinery design and analysis, agricultural machinery management, and other courses that support the department's mission
Demonstrated research activities or industry experience
Interest and ability to successfully participate in co-curricular activities including advise and mentoring of students in curriculum and career planning, involvement in student organizations, internships, and undergraduate research mentoring.
Ability to create effective learning environments where students can succeed and thrive
Ability to effectively communicate and collaborate effectively with colleagues in teaching, research and extension is essential
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, in addition to the ability and desire to work with diverse stakeholders and limited resource beef producers
Evidence of strong analytical, organizational, and communicative skills and collaborative teamwork skills.
Demonstrated ability to secure external research funding.
Ability to successfully pass a background check
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
Knowledge or experience using CAN bus systems
Knowledge of or experience in one or more of the following: engineering simulation tools (FEA,CFD,DEA, etc.), control systems, machine design, welding and metal fabrication techniques.
Experience related to curriculum development in higher education.
Interest and/or experience in developing collaborations with industry partners
Post-doctoral training or additional professional experience beyond the Ph.D. is desirable.
USG Core Values Statement
The University System of Georgia is comprised of our 25 institutions of higher education and learning, as well as the System Office. Our USG Statement of Core Values are Integrity, Excellence, Accountability, and Respect. These values serve as the foundation for all that we do as an organization, and each USG community member is responsible for demonstrating and upholding these standards. More details on the USG Statement of Core Values and Code of Conduct are available in USG Board Policy 8.2.18.1.2 and can be found on-line at https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section8/C224/#p8.2.18_personnel_conduct.
Additionally, USG supports Freedom of Expression as stated in Board Policy 6.5 Freedom of Expression and Academic Freedom found on-line at https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section6/C2653.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Description
The Department of Architecture at the University of Virginia School of Architecture welcomes applications for two endowed faculty fellowships. These two-year, non-tenure-track Assistant Professor General Faculty positions support both research and teaching for emerging practitioners, scholars, or architects seeking to expand their body of work and engage in academia. We seek candidates with a transformative vision for architecture, particularly those with cross-disciplinary interests that connect architecture with landscape architecture, urban design, planning, history and theory, or fields beyond the profession, and that address critical issues of our time.
This is a full-time, two-year appointment, with the expectation that the fellows will reside in Charlottesville and actively engage with faculty, staff, and students at the University. Successful candidates must hold a terminal degree in Architecture (MArch) or a comparable degree in a related design field (such as MLA, MUD, PHD). Faculty fellows are expected to develop a research project and teaching and to present the results of their work in the form of an exhibition in the fall of their second year. Fellows are required to teach four courses per year, including two studios, one required course within the school’s core curriculum, and one elective aligned with their area of research. Fellows will also have the opportunity to participate in committees and other faculty administrative duties.
The Department of Architecture's mission is to educate and inspire the next generation of architectural leaders who understand our discipline as inseparable from the landscapes, cultures, environments, and histories in which we are situated. We actively encourage collaboration across the School of Architecture's disciplines, including with the departments of landscape architecture, urban and environmental planning, and architectural history, as well as with the larger university. As a vital member of this vibrant community, the successful candidate will advance these aims through teaching, research, and collaboration with faculty and students.
The Michael Owen Jones and Robertson Fellowships are structured to provide a gateway into academia and support the development of design research and teaching trajectories. The UVA School of Architecture promotes this by encouraging cross-disciplinary collaboration, providing mentorship, and supporting research development within the school and across the university. Fellows have access to library systems and recently renovated studio, shop, and project spaces, providing state-of-the-art facilities for creative work, scholarly inquiry, and collaborative research (https://www.arch.virginia.edu/about/fablab, https://makergrounds.virginia.edu/).
Qualifiations
Application Instructions
To apply for this position, attach the following:
1) Cover letter. Brief statement that outlines creative practice/research objectives and teaching goals.
2) CV. Full curriculum vitae
3) Portfolio. Digital, including examples of work and teaching (size limit: 100mb)
4) Project Proposal. A one-page outline of the design research project and exhibition.
5) References. Names of three people who can be contacted about your design/academic work.
Applications reviews will begin in late October and will continue to remain open until the position is filled. These positions are not eligible for sponsorship of an H-1B visa requiring consular processing; other visa sponsorships (including H-1B visas not requiring consular processing) may be available, as appropriate. For questions regarding this position, please contact Search Committee Chairs, Professor Matthew Jull at mj5kh@virginia.edu and Department Chair, Professor Jeana Ripple at ripple@virginia.edu. For Interfolio-related assistance, please contact UVA HR.

jobs.title: Open Rank Tenure-line Faculty in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Details
Description
The School of Engineering & Applied Science (SEAS) at the University of Virginia (UVA) seeks candidates for two tenure-eligible or tenured positions in the Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering. The primary responsibilities for this position include research, teaching, and service to the department, university, and professional community. The appointment rank and compensation will be commensurate with experience and qualifications.
Applicants are particularly sought with expertise in hypersonic and high-speed flows, including but not limited to computational and experimental hypersonics, combustion and propulsion, aerothermodynamics and high-temperature gas dynamics, hypersonic materials and structures, hypersonic vehicle design, flight dynamics and control, and data-driven or advanced computational methods for high-speed flow applications. However, outstanding applicants in other areas related to hypersonic and high-speed aerospace systems will also be considered.
The UVA MAE department has strong research expertise in reacting flow, hypersonics, multiphase flow, advanced flow diagnostics, high-performance computing, heat transfer in extreme environments, and robotics and autonomous systems. UVA Engineering has established research thrusts and multidisciplinary centers in several areas of aerospace engineering science and technology, including leadership and participation in the University Consortium for Applied Hypersonics (UCAH), the Rolls-Royce University Technology Center, the Center for Risk Management of Engineering Systems, and the previous National Center for Hypersonic Combined Cycle Propulsion.
This position is based in Charlottesville at our principal location. UVA is a highly selective undergraduate and graduate institution that annually ranks as one of the premiere public universities in the United States, with one of the highest graduation rates in the nation. UVA is situated in Charlottesville, Virginia, a picturesque and vibrant small city consistently recognized as one of the nation's top places to reside. UVA's location offers proximity to the NASA Langley Research Center, NASA Wallops Flight Facility, and many national security stakeholders, enriching opportunities for collaboration and engagement with numerous federal organizations. More information about the city, the school, faculty benefits and other topics can be found at https://hr.virginia.edu/careers-uva/why-uva.
Qualifiations
Candidates must have received a doctorate or equivalent in Aerospace Engineering by the start of their appointment, and an earned B.S. degree in Aerospace Engineering from an ABET-accredited or equivalent program is preferred. Evidence of a commitment to high-impact scholarship, funded research, undergraduate- and graduate-level teaching and advising excellence, professional and university service, and mentoring are expected.
Applicants must demonstrate the potential to pioneer new research frontiers in aerospace science and technology by developing a competitive, externally funded research program. Applicants should demonstrate the potential to collaborate with current UVA faculty in MAE and across the University, including UVA’s School of Engineering and Applied Science, UVA’s School of Arts & Sciences, or UVA’s School of Data Science.
In conjunction with these positions, senior graduate students are eligible and encouraged to consider the UVA Engineering Rising Scholars program. This program is designed to encourage early-career scholars to pursue a career in academia by supporting their postdoctoral work before beginning in a tenure-track position at the University of Virginia. Detailed information and application instructions are available at https://engineering.virginia.edu/rising-scholars-postdoctoral-program.
Application Instructions
Apply for this position in Interfolio. Provide the following in PDF format:
Cover letter that summarizes your areas of research/scholarship, and areas of potential collaboration at the University of Virginia. To help us organize our review of applications, please also specifically list your primary areas of research in boldface at the top of your letter
Curriculum vitae
A statement describing your current research, future directions, and broader impacts;
A statement describing your teaching and mentoring practices, especially in regard to a residential learning environment marked by the free and collegial exchange of ideas;
A statement describing demonstrated contributions to fostering inclusive practices that create climates in which all stakeholders can achieve their maximum potential (please focus on skills and experience, not beliefs and opinions)
You will also request 3-5 references directly in Interfolio by providing names and contact information in the application. These reference requests will be generated immediately once you submit your application.
Review of applications will begin on November 1, 2026 and will continue until the position is filled. The University will perform background checks on all new faculty hires prior to making a final offer of employment.
For questions about these positions, please contact Haibo Dong, Professor, at hd6q@virginia.edu.

Primary Purpose of Organizational Unit:
Established in 1985 by Frank Hawkins Kenan, the Kenan Institute of Private Enterprise is a nonpartisan business policy think tank affiliated with the UNC Kenan-Flagler Business School. The nonprofit institute and its affiliated centers convene leaders from the private sector, academic community and government to build a greater understanding of how entrepreneurship, economic development and global commerce can work for the public good. The institute leverages best-in-class research to develop market-based solutions to today’s most complex economic challenges. In doing so, the institute aims to support businesses and policies that better the lives of people in North Carolina, across the country and around the world.
Position Summary:
The Kenan Institute of Private Enterprise seeks a Research Associate Professor or Research Professor with expertise in applied economics, economic forecasting, regional economics, labor economics, public policy, or related fields to contribute to the North Carolina Advanced Economic Forecasting Initiative (the Initiative). The faculty member will provide intellectual leadership in economic forecasting methodologies, applied economic research, and public-facing analysis for North Carolina. Responsibilities include conducting and disseminating research, developing forecasts and analytical products, communicating findings to academic, business, government, and community audiences, and contributing to the Institute’s mission of translating research into actionable insights. The successful candidate will collaborate with faculty colleagues, research staff, students, and external partners to advance understanding of North Carolina’s economy and support evidence-based decision making.
This position will serve as the Senior Research Economist for the Initiative, and in this role they will lead the development, refinement, validation, and interpretation of economic forecasts, nowcasts, scenario analyses, and related applied research products. Additionally, the Research Associate Professor or Research Professor will work closely with the Executive Director, Director of Research Data Strategy and Analytics, data analysts, faculty affiliates, communications staff, state and local partners, and other Kenan Institute teams to ensure that the Initiative’s economic methodologies and research outputs are rigorous, transparent, actionable, and accessible to both technical and nontechnical audiences.
The role will translate complex economic data and forecasting results into practical insight for policymakers, county leaders, economic developers, business organizations, community colleges, workforce partners, researchers and other stakeholders. The Research Associate Professor or Research Professor will help determine appropriate modeling approaches, evaluate forecast accuracy, communicate uncertainty and limitations, prepare written research products, brief stakeholders, and identify emerging economic issues that warrant additional county-level analysis.
The Research Associate Professor or Research Professor reports to the Executive Director of the Kenan Institute of Private Enterprise (KIPE) and will work in close coordination with the Executive Director, who will lead the Initiative’s strategy, operations, partnerships, stakeholder engagement and public-facing growth. This position may supervise or provide functional guidance to economists, analysts, research staff, students or contractors working on forecasting models, economic analysis, research briefs, county profiles, dashboards or stakeholder deliverables.
The position requires strong technical expertise in applied economics, econometrics, forecasting, regional economics, labor economics, public policy or a related field. The successful candidate will help make the Initiative a trusted, objective, and methodologically sound source of economic intelligence for North Carolina.
This position is contingent upon the continued availability of funding.
Minimum Education and Experience Requirements:
The position requires a Ph.D. (or foreign equivalent) in Economics, Financial Economics, Public Policy, or a related field. The selected candidate can anticipate an initial appointment of Research Associate Professor or Research Professor, depending on credentials.
Preferred Qualifications, Competencies, and Experience:
It is preferred that the successful candidate will possess:
- Experience with county-level, regional, state or local economic data.
- Experience developing or maintaining forecasts, nowcasts, scenario models, economic indicators, composite indexes or regional economic dashboards.
- Experience with GDP, employment, wages, industry composition, workforce skills, housing affordability, tax revenue, migration, business formation or other state and local economic indicators.
- Experience communicating economic analysis to policymakers, local government officials, business leaders, economic developers, workforce partners, media or community audiences.
- Experience working with public data sources such as BEA, BLS, Census, ACS, QCEW, LAUS, Zillow, Freddie Mac, Lightcast, state administrative data or similar datasets.
- Experience evaluating model performance, forecast accuracy, confidence intervals, revisions, scenario ranges or uncertainty communication.
- Experience managing analysts, mentoring junior economists or leading cross-functional applied research teams.
- Familiarity with North Carolina’s economy, regional differences, rural and urban economic development issues, workforce trends, housing markets or local government decision-making.
- Ability to balance academic rigor with practical usefulness for stakeholders.
Campus Security Authority Responsibilities:
Not Applicable.
Special Instructions:
Applicants may view the job posting and follow the application process to be considered at:https://unc.peopleadmin.com/postings/323938.
Applicants should submit a Cover Letter, Curriculum Vitae/Résumé, and Writing/Research Sample. At the time of hire, the selected applicant should be prepared to arrange submission of two (2) signed letters of recommendation, on institutional letterhead, from individuals not affiliated with the Kenan-Flagler Business School.

jobs.title: SUSMAT - Professor in Sensor Technology - Open Rank Position
jobs.description:
About UM6P:
Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P) is an internationally oriented institution of higher learning, that is committed to an educational system based on the highest standards of teaching and research in fields related to the sustainable economic development of Morocco and Africa. UM6P is an institution oriented towards applied research and innovation. On a specific focus on Africa, UM6P aims to position these fields as the forefront and become a university of international standing.
More than just a traditional academic institution, UM6P is a platform for experimentation and a pool of opportunities, for students, professors and staff. It offers a high-quality living and study environment thanks to its state-of-the-art infrastructure. With an innovative approach, UM6P places research and innovation at the heart of its educational project as a driving force of a business model.
In its research approach, the UM6P promotes transdisciplinary, entrepreneurship spirit and collaboration with external institutions for developing up to date science and at continent level in order to address real challenges.
All our programs run as start-ups and can be self-organized when they reach a critical mass. Thus, academic liberty is promoted as far as funding is developed by research teams.
The research programs are integrated from long-term research to short-term applications in linkage with incubation and start-up ecosystems.
About SUSMAT RC:
The Sustainable Materials Research Center (SusMat - RC) is a multidisciplinary research center engaged in the development of advanced biobased products and materials thereof using biotechnological, physical and chemical conversion strategies and engineering processes (b) understanding and controlling their underlying specific functionalities and the structure-properties relationship acting over multiple length scales from the molecular, nano to the macro level and their cross-interactions and (c) utilizing the gathered knowledge and the invented materials to address key technological challenges in Morocco and African continent and assist the transition toward a green and circular economy.
Job Description
The Sustainable Materials Research Center (SUSMAT-RC) at UM6P invites applications for a faculty position in Sensor Technology. Applicants with background in, but not limited to, sensor technology, including sensing principles, sensor design, and applications and those with expertise in one or more of the following areas: MEMS/NEMS, optical sensors, chemical sensors, biosensors, IoT sensors, or other emerging sensing technologies are particularly invited to apply. The successful candidate will plan, develop and conduct applied research projects dedicated to sensor technology, focusing on innovative sensing principles, sensor design with applications in precise agriculture and industrial settings. As a rapidly growing research center, an ideal candidate for this role will be self-motivated, organized, and able to work in ambiguous and changeable situations. A minimum experience of 5 years after the completion of the PhD is required to be eligible for this position.
Key Duties
The successful candidate is expected to have:
Lead all aspects related to Sensor Technology within SUSMAT RC.
Transfer the knowledge and findings related to sensor technology to researchers at UM6P, external clients and/or collaborators when required.
Collaborate with SUSMAT RC researchers through the identification and development of new concepts to be applied to precise agriculture, water quality and their industrial applications thereof.
Design and teach advanced courses related to sensor technology, including sensing principles, sensor design, and applications for the benefit of Master and PhD students at UM6P,
Assist in the delivery of engineering solutions to enable the rapid evolution of applied research through the various TRL levels to development and manufacturing.
Work with members of SUSMAT RC, other faculty members, companies, and different consortia to identify concepts to rapidly test and translate research innovations to products and/or processes for commercialization.
Collaborate with other members of SUSMAT RC in writing manuscripts for publication, filing patents, and developing research proposals to expand research programs consistent with the strategic vision of the center.
Assist in the management and administration of the SUSMAT RC. This activity may include several components, notably (a) collect, analyze, and summarize scientific literature relevant to a given project/technology, (b) develop specific sections in relevant areas of expertise for a given proposal, (c) coordinate the organization of proposal applications in specific area of expertise.
Co-supervise research progress of graduate students and/or postdoctoral fellows. This activity entails regular discussion with group members to ensure they are making progress in their R&D investigations notably in the candidate s area of expertise. Discuss with the director any challenges and roadblocks and ensure that the proposed solutions are implemented and followed upon.
Work with universities, companies, and different consortia to lead groundbreaking R&D for next generation sustainable materials.
Effectively communicate in English (verbally and in writing) to disseminate knowledge to group members, clients, and collaborators and/or to represent the SUSMAT RC at conferences, meetings, and/or workshops.
Proactively engage in collaborative R&D by providing solutions and demonstrating the potential of polymer science and engineering in addressing important Moroccan technology challenges.
Candidate Criteria
To be considered for this role, you will ideally have:
Educational background:
Ph.D. in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, or a closely related field
Experience and Skills:
At least 5 years of professional experience including post-doctoral with recognized expertise in sensor technology, and industrial experience would be a strong asset.
Demonstrated skills in Sensors, Surface Chemistry, Materials Science and Molecular and Nanoscale Science.
sensing technologies, materials, and.
In-depth knowledge of electrochemistry is essential
Good experience with chemical processes and reactions, data analysis techniques,
Demonstrated ability to effectively develop, lead and maintain research programs.
Good teaching experience with the capacity to develop new courses and connect research to teaching (learning by doing) is desirable.
Good experience in the supervision of students from the M.Sc. and Ph.D. programs.
Good leadership and project management skills in driving the full project trajectory from conceptualization to implementation by applying managerial and scientific principles,
Evidence of collaboration with peers at national and/or international institutions,
Familiarity with the institutional and industrial ecosystem of Morocco,
First-hands experience in entrepreneurship, in launching technology start-ups including essential elements such as prototyping/product visualization and early-stage venture funding would be a strong asset,
Awareness of Moroccan/African market and product development opportunities.
Personal Attributes
Be autonomous, detail-oriented, and possess strong organizational skills problem-solving attitudes
Strong initiative, self-motivated, and commitment to achieving quality outputs and excellence.
Demonstrated bounding to diversity and professional integrity.
Demonstrated excellent interpersonal skills and be a good team player
Ability to work effectively with a wide range of individuals, including university professors, industry executives, entrepreneurs, etc
Fluent in English and French, both spoken and written
Application and Selection: The application folder must contain (compressed into 1 pdf file):
Detailed CV,
Cover letter along with a synthetic presentation of the background, research works, projects and activities, publications, key achievements,
Research and teaching plans, entrepreneurial ideas and concepts if any, and services to UM6P community: max 3-4 pages,
Contact information of 3 referees.
Our Offer
Very competitive salary and benefits package.
A unique set of research partners and collaborators.
Access to a pool of highly motivated and rigorously selected Master and PhD students with financial support.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor/Associate Professor in Organizational Leadership – Renewable Contract - 5...
jobs.description:
Job Details
Department/Organization
225101 - School of Leadership & Policy
Rank
Assistant/Associate Professor
Position Summary
The University of Alabama School of Leadership and Policy (SLP) invites applications for multiple renewable contract faculty positions in Organizational Leadership, at the rank of assistant or associate professor, beginning August 2027. We seek teachers and mentors who will help develop leaders across sectors and fields. The SLP will open its doors for classes in fall 2027 as the first new college-level unit established at The University of Alabama in 60 years; as a new school, the SLP offers faculty a rare opportunity to help build curriculum and programs from the ground up.
Detailed Position Information
These are teaching- and student-focused positions. Preparation for this role can come from academic training alone or from a combination of academic training and practical experience. We expect to hire multiple faculty into these positions and understand that an individual candidate may not meet all of the preferences below. We will build a faculty whose strengths are complementary.
Beyond classroom teaching, faculty in these positions will support students directly and will build the school's relationships with the organizations that host and hire them. This work may include career advising and mentoring, supervision of student internships, development of experiential learning programs and courses, identifying capstone clients and internship sites, and connecting students to employers. Assignments are made by the department chair or dean and will reflect the needs of the school and the strengths of each faculty member.
Research is not a condition of these appointments and carries no weight in evaluation, reappointment, or promotion.
Rank at appointment will reflect the candidate's qualifications and experience. Appointments are for a three-year term and are renewable. Reappointment depends on documented performance, continued departmental need, and continued availability of funding. Renewable contract faculty are eligible for promotion in rank.
We offer a competitive salary and relocation assistance.
Minimum Qualifications
Candidates must hold either a doctorate or other terminal degree in a relevant field, or a master's degree combined with a record of professional accomplishment leading or developing organizations.
Candidates must demonstrate strong potential for undergraduate and graduate teaching and for mentoring students. Candidates applying at the associate professor rank should present a record of teaching and professional accomplishment appropriate to that rank.
Preferred Qualifications
Teaching. Applicants should demonstrate the potential to teach in the SLP's Organizational Leadership curriculum, including Foundations of Leadership, Team Dynamics, Ethics in Leadership, and Capstone in Organizational Leadership. Experience directing or teaching a capstone course, or demonstrated aptitude for doing so, is particularly valuable. Relevant teaching experience may have been gained in a university, an agency, the military, or another professional setting. Successful candidates will have the opportunity to develop additional courses that reflect their own expertise and areas of specialization. Professional experience. Candidates whose qualifications are based on practical experience should have held significant responsibility for leading, developing, or advising organizations in government, the military, the nonprofit sector, or private industry. We are particularly interested in candidates who have built leadership development programs, run executive education, or directed organizational change efforts. Mentoring. Applicants should have a record of developing students or junior colleagues. Candidates with practice-based qualifications should also bring a network of contacts who can serve as employers, internship hosts, capstone clients, and guest speakers. Program building. We value candidates who have created something and run it, whether a course sequence, an internship or fellowship program, a training curriculum, or an applied learning program.
Instructions and Required Materials for Application
Applicants should submit a cover letter explaining how their academic training and/or practical experience prepare them to teach and mentor students in organizational leadership. Applicants should also submit a curriculum vitae or resume, a teaching statement, contact information for three references, and graduate transcript (need not be official transcript at this time). The teaching statement should describe the applicant's approach to teaching, prior teaching experience, the courses they are prepared to teach, and what they aim to accomplish with students. Applicants should include any available evidence of teaching effectiveness. Review of applications will begin Nov. 15 and continue until the positions are filled. Questions may be directed to Dr. Joseph L. Smith at jos.smith@ua.edu.
About the Division/College/School
The School of Leadership and Policy (SLP) is the first new college-level unit established at The University of Alabama in 60 years, created to build on the University's history of educating effective leaders and policymakers. UA President Dr. Peter J. Mohler is committed to establishing a nationally recognized institution dedicated to advancing leadership and policy education for the next generation of changemakers. The SLP faculty will blend tenure-track and contract faculty with professors of pp (BA and MPP) and organizational leadership (BA), with plans to add an online BA and in-person and online master's degrees in organizational leadership.
The SLP focuses on leadership across sectors, not partisan politics. Its interdisciplinary, practice-oriented curriculum emphasizes skills, not ideology: ethics, collaboration, data literacy, communication, economic analysis, systems thinking, public problem-solving, and evidence-based practice. The SLP will prepare students of all backgrounds to become effective leaders, policymakers, and public servants who contribute to the social, economic, and civic well-being of Alabama and the nation. Students will be exposed to multiple viewpoints and will engage directly with public institutions, nonprofit organizations, and the private sector through internships, policy labs, and community-based projects, developing the perspective and skills needed to address complex challenges with practical solutions.
As a new school, the SLP offers faculty a rare opportunity: the chance to help build a curriculum, a research culture, and a set of programs from the ground up. The SLP will bring together faculty across leadership and public policy, whose research and teaching will regularly reach practitioners: elected officials, civil servants, and business and nonprofit leaders working to solve real problems. The SLP will be housed in the historic Farrah Hall, now undergoing a $40M renovation to create modern classrooms, offices, and labs.
About the University
The University of Alabama is located in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, named one of Travel + Leisure’s 25 Best College Towns and Cities in the U.S. As one of the nation’s premier universities, UA offers bachelor’s, master's and doctoral degrees in nearly 200 fields of study. With more than 1,400 acres of tree-lined academic core campus and over 300 state-of-the art facilities, UA has been ranked among the most beautiful and most impressive college campuses in the South, in the state of Alabama and in the nation.
In Fall 2023, the Capstone set a new enrollment record with more than 39,000 students, including more than 8,200 in the freshman class. The current enrollment includes students from every county in Alabama, every state in the nation and 92 countries around the world. More than 1,100 National Merit Scholars are currently enrolled, making UA one of the largest enrolling institutions of the scholars in the country.
UA was recently recognized as a Top Producing Institution of Fulbright U.S. students for the seventh time in nine years, as well as a Top Producing Institution of Fulbright U.S. Scholars for the first time. UA is one of only 12 universities in the nation to receive both honors.
For reasons like this, the University made Forbes list of America’s Top Colleges for 2023 and Time magazine’s list of Top 50 Best Colleges for Future Leaders. It also made Princeton Review’s list of Top Value Colleges.
UA is also designated among the top doctoral research universities in the United States in the Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education. One of the fastest growing major research institutions in the nation, UA saw a 21% increase in sponsored awards in the 2023 fiscal year.
Since 2015, UA has invested over $1.1 billion in the physical campus, adding more than 2.55 million gross square feet of space, over 150 new research-intensive faculty, signature research areas (e.g., “The Alabama Research Institutes”), and a growing number of partnerships with industry and with state and federal agencies.
The University employs nearly 2,100 faculty and over 4,500 staff, with 52 UA researchers included in the National Academy of Inventors. An additional 40 current faculty have received the NSF CAREER Award, the nation’s most prestigious recognition of top performing young scientists in disciplines ranging from nanoscience and engineering to biological sciences.

Department/Organization
225101 - School of Leadership & Policy
Rank
Assistant/Associate Professor
Position Summary
The University of Alabama School of Leadership and Policy (SLP) invites applications for multiple renewable contract faculty positions in Public Policy, at the rank of assistant or associate professor, beginning August 2027. We seek teachers and mentors who will prepare students to analyze, shape, and carry out public policy. The SLP will open its doors for classes in fall 2027 as the first new college-level unit established at The University of Alabama in 60 years; as a new school, the SLP offers faculty a rare opportunity to help build a curriculum and set of programs from the ground up.
Detailed Position Information
These are teaching- and student-focused appointments in the undergraduate and graduate public policy programs. Preparation for this role can come from academic training alone or from a combination of academic training and practical experience. We expect to hire multiple faculty into these positions and understand that an individual candidate may not meet all of the preferences below. We will build a faculty whose strengths are complementary.
Beyond classroom teaching, faculty in these positions will support students directly and will build the school's relationships with the organizations that host and hire them. This work may include career advising and mentoring, supervision of the public policy capstone and student internships, development of experiential learning programs and courses, identifying capstone clients and internship sites, and connecting students to employers. Assignments are made by the department chair or dean and will reflect the needs of the school and the strengths of each faculty member.
Research is not a condition of these appointments and carries no weight in evaluation, reappointment, or promotion.
Rank at appointment will reflect the candidate's qualifications and experience. Appointments are for a three-year term and are renewable. Reappointment depends on documented performance, continued departmental need, and continued availability of funding. Renewable contract faculty are eligible for promotion in rank.
We offer a competitive salary and relocation assistance.
Minimum Qualifications
Candidates must hold either a doctorate or other terminal degree in a relevant field, or a master's degree combined with a record of professional accomplishment in public policy. Relevant doctoral fields include public policy, public administration, economics, political science, and related disciplines in the social sciences. We also welcome candidates whose doctoral training lies elsewhere but whose research and teaching bear directly on public policy.
All candidates must demonstrate strong potential for undergraduate and graduate teaching and for mentoring students. Candidates applying at the associate professor rank should present a record of teaching and professional accomplishment appropriate to that rank.
Preferred Qualifications
Teaching. Applicants should demonstrate the potential to teach in the SLP's public policy curriculum at the undergraduate and graduate levels. Courses include Economics of Public Policy, Policy Analysis and Evaluation, Research Methods in Public Policy, Values in Public Policy, Communicating Public Policy, the Policymaking Process, and Leadership in Public Policy. Experience directing or teaching a capstone course in public policy, or demonstrated aptitude for doing so, is particularly valuable. Successful candidates will help build out the curriculum by developing additional courses that reflect their own expertise and areas of specialization. Policy expertise. We welcome candidates whose expertise bears on the policy challenges facing Alabama and its communities. That expertise may have been developed through scholarship, professional practice, or both. Analytic preparation. We are particularly interested in candidates prepared to teach the analytic core of the curriculum, including policy analysis and evaluation, economics for public policy, and the research methods sequence. Professional experience. Candidates whose qualifications are based on practical experience should have led the design, adoption, implementation, or evaluation of public policy in government, the military, the nonprofit sector, or private industry. Mentoring. We seek candidates who are committed to student development and who show evidence of it, whether through teaching, advising, supervising, coaching, or developing junior colleagues. Candidates coming from practice will often bring a network of contacts who can serve as employers, internship hosts, capstone clients, and guest speakers. Program building. We value candidates who have created something and run it, whether a course sequence, an internship or fellowship program, a training curriculum, or an applied learning program.
Instructions and Required Materials for Application
Applicants should submit a cover letter explaining how their academic training, practical experience, or both prepare them to teach and mentor students in public policy. Applicants should also submit a curriculum vitae or resume, a teaching statement, contact information for three references, and graduate transcript (need not be official transcript at this time). The teaching statement should describe the applicant's approach to teaching, prior teaching experience, the courses they are prepared to teach, and what they aim to accomplish with students. Applicants should include any available evidence of teaching effectiveness. Review of applications will begin Nov. 15 and continue until the positions are filled. Questions may be directed to Dr. Joseph L. Smith at jos.smith@ua.edu.
About the Division/College/School
The School of Leadership and Policy (SLP) is the first new college-level unit established at The University of Alabama in 60 years, created to build on the University's history of educating effective leaders and policymakers. UA President Dr. Peter J. Mohler is committed to establishing a nationally recognized institution dedicated to advancing leadership and policy education for the next generation of changemakers. The SLP faculty will blend tenure-track and contract faculty with professors of pp (BA and MPP) and organizational leadership (BA), with plans to add an online BA and in-person and online master's degrees in organizational leadership.
The SLP focuses on leadership across sectors, not partisan politics. Its interdisciplinary, practice-oriented curriculum emphasizes skills, not ideology: ethics, collaboration, data literacy, communication, economic analysis, systems thinking, public problem-solving, and evidence-based practice. The SLP will prepare students of all backgrounds to become effective leaders, policymakers, and public servants who contribute to the social, economic, and civic well-being of Alabama and the nation. Students will be exposed to multiple viewpoints and will engage directly with public institutions, nonprofit organizations, and the private sector through internships, policy labs, and community-based projects, developing the perspective and skills needed to address complex challenges with practical solutions.
As a new school, the SLP offers faculty a rare opportunity: the chance to help build a curriculum, a research culture, and a set of programs from the ground up. The SLP will bring together faculty across leadership and public policy, whose research and teaching will regularly reach practitioners: elected officials, civil servants, and business and nonprofit leaders working to solve real problems. The SLP will be housed in the historic Farrah Hall, now undergoing a $40M renovation to create modern classrooms, offices, and labs.
About the University
The University of Alabama is located in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, named one of Travel + Leisure’s 25 Best College Towns and Cities in the U.S. As one of the nation’s premier universities, UA offers bachelor’s, master's and doctoral degrees in nearly 200 fields of study. With more than 1,400 acres of tree-lined academic core campus and over 300 state-of-the art facilities, UA has been ranked among the most beautiful and most impressive college campuses in the South, in the state of Alabama and in the nation.
In Fall 2023, the Capstone set a new enrollment record with more than 39,000 students, including more than 8,200 in the freshman class. The current enrollment includes students from every county in Alabama, every state in the nation and 92 countries around the world. More than 1,100 National Merit Scholars are currently enrolled, making UA one of the largest enrolling institutions of the scholars in the country.
UA was recently recognized as a Top Producing Institution of Fulbright U.S. students for the seventh time in nine years, as well as a Top Producing Institution of Fulbright U.S. Scholars for the first time. UA is one of only 12 universities in the nation to receive both honors.
For reasons like this, the University made Forbes list of America’s Top Colleges for 2023 and Time magazine’s list of Top 50 Best Colleges for Future Leaders. It also made Princeton Review’s list of Top Value Colleges.
UA is also designated among the top doctoral research universities in the United States in the Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education. One of the fastest growing major research institutions in the nation, UA saw a 21% increase in sponsored awards in the 2023 fiscal year.
Since 2015, UA has invested over $1.1 billion in the physical campus, adding more than 2.55 million gross square feet of space, over 150 new research-intensive faculty, signature research areas (e.g., “The Alabama Research Institutes”), and a growing number of partnerships with industry and with state and federal agencies.
The University employs nearly 2,100 faculty and over 4,500 staff, with 52 UA researchers included in the National Academy of Inventors. An additional 40 current faculty have received the NSF CAREER Award, the nation’s most prestigious recognition of top performing young scientists in disciplines ranging from nanoscience and engineering to biological sciences.

jobs.title: Faculty Position in Clinical Psychology, Department of Psychology, College of Arts and Sciences
jobs.description:
Faculty Position in Clinical Psychology, Department of Psychology, College of Arts and Sciences
Employer: American University of Sharjah
Location: Sharjah, United Arab Emirates
Start date: August 2027 (a later start may be negotiated)
Position type: Open rank, full-time (part-time can be considered)
Position Description
The Department of Psychology at American University of Sharjah (AUS) invites applications for a full-time faculty position in clinical psychology to begin in August 2027. The appointee will play a leading role in establishing the department's planned master's degree program in clinical psychology, which is intended to admit its first cohort in Fall 2028, and will be a founding member of the program's faculty.
The program is being designed as a practice-oriented, evidence-based degree that integrates supervised clinical experience with coursework from an early stage, makes use of new technologies in clinical training and gives sustained attention to the cultural and linguistic context of clinical practice in the UAE and the wider region. It will be the first clinical psychology master's degree program in the Emirate of Sharjah.
A defining emphasis of the program will be cross-cultural clinical competence. Most of the evidence base in clinical psychology was developed in Western, English-speaking populations, while the UAE is home to more than 200 nationalities and a largely multilingual client population. The program will therefore train students to evaluate, adapt and validate assessment instruments and intervention protocols for new, non-Western contexts, and to practice competently across cultures, languages and religious traditions. Candidates with research or clinical experience adapting psychological assessments and interventions to non-Western settings are particularly encouraged to apply.
The appointee will contribute to the design of the curriculum; help build placement partnerships with mental health services in Sharjah and the wider UAE; teach graduate and undergraduate courses in clinical psychology; supervise student clinical work if licensed; and maintain an active program of research. The appointee will work closely with the department head and the program planning committee, and will be eligible to apply for director of the program.
Two Profiles
The department welcomes applications from candidates with either of the following profiles. Both are needed for the program to succeed, and the rank and terms of appointment will reflect the candidate's qualifications and experience.
Clinical or counseling psychologists with a doctoral degree (PhD or PsyD) and a strong record of research and publication, at the rank of Assistant Professor, Associate Professor or Professor, who will help lead the program academically and supervise graduate research Practicing clinical or counseling psychologists with a PhD or PsyD who hold a license to practice in the UAE, or are eligible for one (check your eligibility with the relevant health authority before applying) who bring supervisory experience; appointment may be at the rank of Assistant Professor, Associate Professors or Professor of Practice Required Qualifications
A PhD or PsyD in clinical or counseling psychology or a closely related field A record of, or clear potential for, excellence in teaching at the graduate level A commitment to research, teaching and service appropriate to the rank sought Fluency in English as the language of instruction Preferred Qualifications
A current license to practice psychology in the UAE or eligibility for one Experience supervising trainee clinicians in health service settings Experience designing, launching or accrediting graduate programs in clinical psychology Research or clinical experience with internet-delivered interventions, simulation-based training or the cultural adaptation of assessment instruments and treatments Proficiency in Arabic Experience in American-style higher education The Department
The Department of Psychology offers the Bachelor of Arts in Psychology and a minor in psychology, and is growing rapidly. Faculty research spans clinical and counseling psychology, cognitive psychology, cultural psychology, psycholinguistics, social psychology and work and organizational psychology. The department has five laboratory spaces for research with human participants, a research participation pool supported by Sona Systems, and dedicated technical and administrative support. The planned master's degree program will be the department's first graduate program.
Application Instructions
Applicants should submit the following through the online application form at https://acg-apps1.aus.edu/cas/empapp/apply.php?p=PSY-27-01:
A curriculum vitae (PDF) A letter describing the applicant's interest in the position, which of the two profiles the applicant best fits, and, where relevant, the applicant's licensure status (and eligibility for licensing) in the UAE or elsewhere The names and contact details of three referees Review of applications will begin January 15, 2027 and continue until the position is filled. Questions about the position, the planned program or life in the UAE may be directed to the search committee chair, Tatiana Tairi, at ttairi@aus.edu.
About American University of Sharjah
American University of Sharjah (AUS) invites applications from accomplished scholars committed to excellence in teaching, learning and research within an American-style, globally recognized institution. Successful candidates will be offered a salary commensurate with experience, along with free housing, paid utilities and other attractive benefits.
As a comprehensive, independent, non-profit, coeducational university, AUS is consistently ranked among the top 10 universities in the Arab region and among the top 17 percent of ranked universities in the world (QS, 2027). The university fosters a diverse community of over 6,000 students from more than 100 nations, with English as the language of instruction and the workplace.
Located in Sharjah's University City, AUS is directly adjacent to the Sharjah Research, Technology and Innovation Park, providing faculty with significant opportunities to engage in interdisciplinary research and contribute directly to the UAE's rapidly expanding innovation ecosystem. The campus is set in a vibrant and cosmopolitan area, offering abundant opportunities for travel, entertainment and cultural experiences, with Sharjah International Airport minutes away and Dubai International Airport only 30 minutes from campus. A number of schools aligned with various international curricula are located nearby.
AUS is licensed and its programs are accredited by the Commission for Academic Accreditation of the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research of the United Arab Emirates. AUS has been accredited in the United States of America by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education (1007 North Orange Street, 4th Floor, MB #166, Wilmington, DE 19801 USA) since June 2004.
For more information, please visit www.aus.edu.

Graduate degree programs include: MS and PhD in Biology, MS and PhD in Bioinformatics, MS and PhD in Computational Science and Engineering, PhD in Neuroscience & Neurotechnology, as well as a PhD in Quantitative Biosciences, Ocean Sciences and Engineering, and Dual Doctor of Physical Therapy/Doctor of Philosophy. Job Summary As part of a new College of Sciences initiative, Georgia Tech for Georgia's Tomorrow (GT2), the Georgia Institute of Technology invites applications for two tenure-track faculty positions in: 1) Ecology and 2) Coastal processes, with a preference to the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor. The U.S. Southeast region, including Georgia, is undergoing rapid environmental and land use change that have far-reaching effects on human and ecological systems. Thus, GT2 was created to address major challenges at the intersection of environmental and community resilience, by aligning discovery science, technological innovation, and AI-enabled decision tools to address urgent challenges.
Responsibilities
In Ecology, we seek candidates who will make fundamental contributions to understanding how organisms respond to environmental change, with a particular interest in research that incorporates a behavioral perspective. Relevant research might investigate how human land use changes (e.g., urbanization) or climate change shape animal behavior, movement, foraging, and social dynamics in ways that affect biodiversity and ecosystem function. This hire will advance our ability to use adaptively manage ecosystems to maintain biodiversity and continue to provide ecosystem services to people.
For Coastal Processes, we are seeking candidates who will make fundamental contributions in the broadly-defined area of coastal processes through a range of methodological approaches, and whose research program addresses coastal resilience and solutions. Areas of particular interest include, but are not limited to, coastal and nearshore oceanography, physical hydrology of surface and subsurface water, coastal geomorphology, and coastal hazards such as flooding and subsidence.
Required Qualifications
An earned doctorate is required by the start of the appointment.
Preferred Qualifications
The successful candidates will complement the existing expertise within the College of Sciences (https://cos.gatech.edu/). Strengths in computational modeling, artificial intelligence and machine learning, and remote sensing are highly desirable. Applicants will be considered at all ranks with priority given to exceptional candidates at the assistant or early-associate professor stage. Candidates are expected to demonstrate an exceptional commitment to the teaching and mentoring of students.
Required Documents to Attach
Applicants should submit a letter of application, curriculum vitae, a statement of research interests, a description of teaching/ mentoring philosophy including the potential for contributions to GT's mission and values, and the names and contact information for at least three references. In their application, faculty candidates should describe how they will contribute to GT2 by performing research that boosts resilience, reduces risk, and enables growth, with a demonstrative impact on communities of the U.S. Southeast region. Application materials should be submitted as one PDF file via the Georgia Tech online portal https://hr.gatech.edu/careers.An earned doctorate is required by the start of the appointment, and a background check must be completed prior to beginning employment.

Job Summary

Position # 20007558
Augusta University's Medical College of Georgia, Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology is seeking a faculty member at the rank of Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor, as an experienced OB-GYN. The selected candidate will be responsible for testing, diagnosing, treating, and monitoring diseases and issues related to women's health, providing medical counsel and support to women during pregnancy and childbirth, and providing inpatient/outpatient obstetrics and gynecology services throughout assigned clinic locations, including infant delivery and related surgical procedures. This position does not meet the requirements to be on a tenure track.
Responsibilities
Clinical Responsibilities - 90%
Performing a wide range of tests, including pap smears, pelvic, and breast exams
Diagnosing and prescribing treatments for disorders and diseases
Conducting routine check-ups on patients
Monitoring and treating expectant mothers during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum
Recording medical histories
Educating patients about disease prevention and detection, and reproductive health
Collaborating with other medical and non-medical personnel
Keeping up to date with current practices and innovations
Provide clinical coverage and resident supervision in Labor and Delivery
Provision of patient care in ambulatory setting and in surgical theater
Resident Education - 10%
Education of residents/students and supervision is included when in ambulatory setting and surgery
Required Qualifications
MD or equivalent. Must be licensed or eligible for license in the state of Georgia and have current DEA. Must be board-certified or board eligible as well as eligible for an active Georgia State medical license.
Assistant Professor- Early level career as a faculty member with appropriate post graduate training.
Associate Professor- Mid level career faculty member with at least five years at rank of Assistant Professor or comparable training, background, and experience.
Professor- Senior level career faculty member with at least five years at the rank of Associate Professor or comparable training, background, and experience.

- Successful experience (which will necessarily be waived for those just entering the academic profession who meet all other requirements); and,
- Desirable personal qualities judged on the basis of personal interview, complete biographical data, and recommendations.

This position is fiscal year based and works year-round.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Open Rank/Open Tenure - Small Animal Educator, Harvey S. Peeler Jr. College of Veterinary Medicine
Clemson University: Harvey S. Peeler Jr. College of Veterinary Medicine
Location: CVM - COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE HUB(001184) BLDG001184
Open Date: Sep 22, 2026
Description
The Clemson University Harvey S. Peeler Jr. College of Veterinary Medicine (PCVM) is seeking applicants for several full-time positions to serve as Small Animal Educators. These faculty positions will play a pivotal role in the development and implementation of the Clemson DVM curriculum (https://www.clemson.edu/veterinary-medicine/students/curriculum.html). The successful candidates will have a primary instructional role in developing and delivering small animal medicine and / or surgery content in the integrated Clemson DVM curriculum. These faculty members will teach with a dynamic, collaborative team consisting of experienced general practice clinicians, boarded specialists, and education specialists. The small animal medicine and surgery course series is designed to be an integrated, systems-based approach for conditions common to small animal general practice. This role is designed to attract outstanding educators and experienced clinicians who are passionate about teaching diagnostic medicine and small animal surgery in a practical, integrated fashion. Board certification in small animal internal medicine, small animal surgery, or ABVP certification is encouraged but not required. The Clemson DVM curriculum is based upon integrative, collaborative team teaching in which faculty with varying backgrounds can work together to offer students an inclusive and innovative learning environment. The Small Animal Educators will collaborate with our other teaching faculty to facilitate vertical and horizontal integration for the delivery of core small animal internal medicine and surgery principles. Utilizing state of the art classrooms and teaching technology, this faculty member will be asked to adopt an integrated educational approach to provide students with a strong foundation of cognitive, clinical, and professional competencies in preparation for entry into the partially distributive model of clinical training in the fourth year. This position will consist primarily of didactic and small group instruction, along with some instruction in teaching laboratories. While the PCVM will not have a specialty referral hospital, it will have a fully staffed Community Practice as well as a robust Shelter Medicine spay-neuter program. The Small Animal Educators will work closely with the Community Practice and Shelter Medicine clinicians to integrate classroom concepts that translate seamlessly into real world experiences. A clinical service commitment is not required; however, interested individuals are encouraged to engage in teaching activities in our Community Practice. Additionally, these faculty members will engage in scholarly activity, which can include curriculum development, programmatic or curricular assessment, scholarship of teaching and learning, and other similar activities. Finally, a hybrid academic appointment will be considered for a boarded small animal specialist (internal medicine and / or surgery). If desired, this individual may seek a combination of a part-time academic appointment at Clemson while also having a part-time position in private referral practice. The possibility of a 9-month to 12-month contract are options that can be discussed with the Department Chair. Overview of Clemson and the PCVM Located in South Carolina's beautiful and fast-growing Upstate, Clemson University is the land-grant university of South Carolina and ranks among the country's top 50 national public universities in the U.S. News & World Report. The University has nearly 23,400 students (including nearly 18,600 undergraduates) who can select from 80 undergraduate and 110 graduate degree programs. Clemson employs over 1,150 full-time faculty and has an annual budget expenditure of over $900M. Clemson University maintains its status as an R1 Carnegie Research Institution while maintaining a strong focus on undergraduate education. The PCVM is currently seeking accreditation by the American Veterinary Medicine Association-Council on Education to offer the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine degree to approximately 80 students per cohort which started in August 2026). The PCVM plans to utilize a partial distributive model of clinical training for students. Its brand-new state of the art campus will reside in Pendleton, SC, near the T. Ed Garrison Arena, will house research and teaching labs, and utilize both ambulatory services as well as teaching sites at the Clemson University Equine Center, Lamaster Dairy Cattle Center, and other locations for education in the field. In 2023, the Board of Trustees approved Clemson Elevate, the university's new strategic plan. Clemson Elevate is built on 3 pillars: deliver the #1 student experience, double research by 2035, and transform lives statewide and beyond. The PCVM was named as a strategic priority for the university, demonstrating the importance of the new college to the future of the university and the state. We are excited to attract a team of top talent as we build the new college. Overview of the Position Reporting to the Department Chair and working closely with the Foundational Sciences and Clinical Skills Leads, the small animal medicine educator will: Create and deliver the small animal content in the team-taught systems-based courses in the curriculum. Participate in teaching laboratories as agreed upon with colleagues and the department chair Develop assessment strategies in alignment with the overall competency-based curriculum. Collaborate with other faculty members to ensure integration of knowledge and skills across years and courses. Actively and effectively engage in student-centered instruction, coaching, and mentorship. Collaborate closely with the Clemson University Community Practice and with our partner clinics. Serve on PCVM and campus committees as an appointed or elected member. Additionally, the faculty member must have the ability to: Emulate our PCVM cultural values including integrity, authenticity, respect, welcoming, trust, and collaboration. Work independently and collaboratively as part of a team, possess exemplary verbal and written communication skills, with exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail. Prioritize and manage multiple tasks, meet deadlines, and function independently with limited supervision and guidance. Work in partnership with faculty and staff across multiple disciplines and functions across the college and university. Participate in research and scholarship initiatives designed to improve educational and professional outcomes. Demonstrate a commitment to the core values of Clemson University and specifically to community, engagement, belonging and accessibility (CEBA).
Qualifications
DVM or equivalent with 3+ years of relevant experience.
Applicants must demonstrate a strong foundation in small animal practice and the ability to teach clinical skills to veterinary students in classroom and laboratory/skills settings
Board certification is not required; board-eligible/board-certified candidates are encouraged to apply.
Commitment to excellence and creativity in education.
Licensed or eligible for licensure to practice veterinary medicine in South Carolina and ability to obtain a DEA license.
Preferred qualifications include:
5+ years of relevant experience in veterinary medicine or education.
Experience in clinical skills education, simulation pedagogy, and/or competency-based assessment.
Demonstrated experience mentoring learners (students, interns, residents, or technicians).
Board certification or residency training in small animal medicine (ACVIM, ECVIM), small animal surgery (ACVS, ECVS) or American Board of Veterinary Practitioners (ABVP).
Application Instructions
Applications and nominations will be accepted until the position is filled. Interested parties must apply electronically in Interfolio:
https://apply.interfolio.com/194184
and submit a cover letter, resume, and contact information for three references by 10/23/26 to assure full consideration.
For questions regarding this position, please email Dr. Jonathan Fogle at fogle7@clemson.edu
For more information and to apply, visit https://apply.interfolio.com/194184

jobs.description:
Job Details
Assistant Professor - Systems Neurophysiology
Date Posted: 09/21/2026
Closing Date: 11/16/2026, 11:59PM ET
Req ID: 48726
Job Category: Faculty - Tenure Stream (continuing)
Faculty/Division: Faculty of Arts & Science
Department: Cell and Systems Biology
Campus: St. George (Downtown Toronto)
Existing Vacancy: Yes
Position Description
The Department of Cell & Systems Biology in the Faculty of Arts & Science at the University of Toronto invites applications for a full-time tenure stream position in Systems Neurophysiology. The appointment will be at the rank of Assistant Professor, with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027.
Requirements and Qualifications
Candidates must have earned a PhD degree in Biology or a related area by the time of appointment, with a demonstrated record of excellence in research and teaching in Systems Neurophysiology. We seek candidates whose research and teaching interests address fundamental questions in Systems Neurophysiology that will complement and enhance our existing departmental strengths in neuroscience, genomics, cell and developmental biology, molecular biology, and bioinformatics.
Candidates must provide evidence of research excellence which can be demonstrated through a record of publications in top-ranked and field-relevant journals or forthcoming publications that meet high international standards; the submitted research statement; presentations at significant conferences; awards and accolades; and strong endorsements from referees.
Evidence of excellence in teaching will be demonstrated through teaching accomplishments, the teaching dossier (including the required materials outlined below, as well as evidence of superior performance in other teaching-related activities), and strong letters of reference. Other teaching-related activities can include performance as a teaching assistant or course instructor, experience leading successful workshops or seminars, student mentorship, or excellent conference presentations or posters.
Responsibilities
The successful candidate will be expected to pursue innovative and independent research, and to establish an outstanding, competitive, and externally funded research program.
In addition, the successful candidate will be assigned a teaching and service load.
Hiring Salary Range
The expected salary range is $125,000-175,000 CAD per annum, depending on experience. Negotiations beyond this salary range will be considered for exceptionally qualified candidates.
About Us
The Department of Cell & Systems Biology (CSB) at the University of Toronto is a vibrant and highly collaborative scientific community that pursues innovative research in molecular life sciences, systems biology and biology education.
We investigate the behaviour of cells – the fundamental units of life – in terms of molecular processes within and between cells. Our researchers integrate both hypothesis-driven and discovery-based strategies to gain a mechanistic understanding of complex and highly dynamic cellular systems and how they govern the development, physiology, and evolution of organisms.
CSB is home to a world-class research ecosystem providing access to state-of-the-art platforms in neurophysiology, high-throughput genomics, advanced cellular imaging, chemical biology, proteomics, and computational modeling. These systems contribute to new methodologies for studying the fundamental biological mechanisms that govern interactions at all levels of complexity, ranging from molecules to communities.
For more information on working at the University of Toronto, please visit https://www.utoronto.ca/research-innovation/working-at-uoft.
This search aligns with the University’s commitment to strategically and proactively promote diversity among our community members (Statement on Equity, Diversity & Excellence). Recognizing that Black, Indigenous, and other Racialized communities have experienced inequities that have developed historically and are ongoing, we strongly welcome and encourage candidates from those communities to apply.
Application Process
All application materials, including recent reference letters, must be received by November 16, 2026.
All qualified candidates are invited to apply online by clicking the link below. Your CV and cover letter should be uploaded into the dedicated fields. Please combine additional application materials into one or two files in PDF/MS Word format. Applicants must submit the following materials:
a cover letter;
a current curriculum vitae;
a research statement outlining current and future research interests (3-5 pages);
a recent writing sample, for example a published or submitted manuscript;
a teaching dossier, including
a teaching statement,
sample course materials, and
teaching evaluations or evidence of superior performance in other teaching-related activities as listed above; and
the name and contact information of three references.
The University of Toronto’s recruiting tool will automatically solicit and collect letters of reference from each referee within 48 hours of an application being submitted. Applicants remain responsible for ensuring that referees submit recent letters (on letterhead, dated and signed) by the closing date. Submission guidelines and details on the automatic reference letter collection, including timelines, are available in the candidate FAQ.
If you have any questions about this position, please contact csbsearch@utoronto.ca.
All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority.
Diversity Statement
The University of Toronto embraces Diversity and is building a culture of belonging that increases our capacity to effectively address and serve the interests of our global community. We strongly encourage applications from Indigenous Peoples, Black and racialized persons, women, persons with disabilities, and people of diverse sexual and gender identities. We value applicants who have demonstrated a commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion and recognize that diverse perspectives, experiences, and expertise are essential to strengthening our academic mission.
As part of your application, you will be asked to complete a brief Diversity Survey. This survey is voluntary. Any information directly related to you is confidential and cannot be accessed by search committees or human resources staff. Results will be aggregated for institutional planning purposes. For more information, please see http://uoft.me/UP.
Accessibility Statement
The University strives to be an equitable and inclusive community, and proactively seeks to increase diversity among its community members. Our values regarding equity and diversity are linked with our unwavering commitment to excellence in the pursuit of our academic mission.
The University is committed to the principles of the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). As such, we strive to make our recruitment, assessment and selection processes as accessible as possible and provide accommodations as required for applicants with disabilities.
If you require any accommodations at any point during the application and hiring process, please contact uoft.careers@utoronto.ca.
