Position Summary
The University of Alabama invites applications and nominations for the position of Associate Program Director and faculty in its developing Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) program. Pending approval by The Board of Trustees of The University of Alabama and authorization by the Commission on Accreditation in Physical Therapy Education (CAPTE), the DPT program will address a distinct workforce need while drawing from a strong pipeline of qualified students. We seek an entrepreneurial, collaborative, and student-centered physical therapist educator, clinician, scholar, and academic leader who will partner with the Program Director to build a nationally distinctive program aligned with the College of Community Health Sciences’ mission and expand access to high-quality physical therapy services, particularly in rural and underserved communities across Alabama and the Southeast. The Associate Program Director will provide operational and academic leadership across curriculum development and delivery, faculty and student support, assessment, accreditation readiness, and strategic program growth. The successful candidate will also teach in areas aligned with their expertise; advise and mentor students; maintain an appropriate record of scholarship, clinical engagement, and service; and represent the program within the College, University, profession, and community. CCHS is vibrant and growing, with academic programs in Rural Community Health, Population Health Sciences, Translational Science and Medicine, and additional health-professions programs in development. CCHS is home to a nationally renowned Sports Medicine Clinic and Fellowship, as well as Family and Psychiatry residencies and multiple fellowships. Appointments to the faculty of The University of Alabama are based on the personnel requirements of the University’s academic programs and on the goal of achieving and maintaining excellence in its teaching, research, and service/academic citizenship activities.
Detailed Position Information
Associate Program Director, Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT)—Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor; tenure-track/tenured or clinical track, commensurate with qualifications.
Reporting to and working closely with the Program Director, the Associate Program Director will help lead the planning, implementation, evaluation, and continuous improvement of the developing DPT program. Primary responsibilities may include coordinating day-to-day academic operations; supporting curriculum design, sequencing, integration, and review; facilitating faculty collaboration and development; contributing to faculty workload and course planning; coordinating student progression, advising, remediation, and success initiatives; supporting admissions and recruitment; overseeing collection and analysis of program outcomes; maintaining documentation for CAPTE candidacy and accreditation; contributing to policy development and implementation; and representing the Program Director when delegated or in the Director’s absence.
The Associate Program Director will collaborate with the Program Director, Director of Clinical Education, faculty, staff, College leadership, and external partners to ensure alignment among didactic education, clinical education, student outcomes, and workforce needs. Additional responsibilities include classroom, laboratory, simulation, or clinical instruction; student mentorship; scholarship appropriate to rank and track; development of clinical and community partnerships; and service to the program, College, University, profession, and community.
Minimum Qualifications
• Earned terminal academic or clinical doctorate (with clinical specialty certification) from an institution recognized by the U.S. Department of Education or an equivalent international credential.
• Physical therapist licensed in a U.S. jurisdiction and eligible for licensure in Alabama.
• Minimum of five years of full-time or equivalent experience in physical therapist education, including teaching and academic leadership responsibilities.
• Evidence of contemporary expertise relevant to an entry-level DPT curriculum.
• Demonstrated experience with curriculum development, program assessment, student progression, faculty collaboration, or academic operations.
• Demonstrated ability to lead collaboratively, manage multiple priorities, communicate effectively, and support colleagues and students in a developing program.
• Evidence of excellence in teaching, student mentorship, scholarship, and service.
• Qualifications commensurate with appointment at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor rank and the applicable tenure or clinical track.
Preferred Qualifications
• Prior experience as an associate program director, program director, department chair, academic coordinator, or in a comparable leadership role in a professional physical therapy program. • Substantive knowledge of CAPTE standards, candidacy requirements, accreditation processes, and continuous quality improvement. • Experience with curriculum mapping, instructional design, faculty workload planning, student assessment, remediation, and program outcome assessment. • Experience developing and implementing academic policies, procedures, and operational systems. • Record of scholarship, clinical practice, or externally supported work appropriate to rank and track. • Expertise in one or more areas that complement the developing curriculum. • Experience with interprofessional education, community-engaged practice, rural health, or service to underserved populations. • Experience developing clinical, health-system, educational, or community partnerships. • Active engagement in the American Physical Therapy Association or related professional organizations. • Mission-driven, collaborative, organized, and outcomes-oriented leadership style. • Commitment to academic excellence, student success, professional formation, and a respectful learning and working environment.
Instructions and Required Materials for Application
1. Cover letter addressing qualifications, academic leadership experience, and interest in serving as Associate Program Director of a developing DPT program. 2. Curriculum vitae. 3. Leadership statement describing the candidate’s approach to collaborative program administration, curriculum quality, faculty support, student success, and accreditation readiness. 4. Teaching statement describing educational philosophy, instructional experience, and approach to student learning and mentorship. 5. Statement of scholarly, clinical, or professional agenda appropriate to the candidate’s rank and track. 6. Names and contact information for three professional references; references will be contacted only with the candidate’s consent.
About the Division/College/School
The College of Community Health Sciences (CCHS) was founded in 1972 by William Willard, MD, author of the “Willard Report” and considered the “Father of Family Medicine,” with a mandate to train family physicians for Alabama, particularly its rural areas. The DCE will also teach in areas of expertise, advise and mentor students, participate as a core faculty member in curriculum and program governance, contribute to scholarship and service consistent with appointment and rank, and help expand clinical partnerships that support rural and underserved communities.
Minimum Qualifications
• Physical therapist who is licensed and in good standing in a U.S. jurisdiction and is eligible for physical therapist licensure in Alabama.
• Earned academic doctoral degree from an institution recognized by the U.S. Department of Education; a DPT degree alone may be considered when accompanied by additional academic credentials, specialization, or a record of scholarly achievement appropriate to the appointment and institutional requirements.
• Minimum of five (5) years of full-time or equivalent experience as a physical therapist, including substantive clinical practice and experience in physical therapist clinical education as a clinical instructor, site coordinator of clinical education, DCE, assistant DCE, or comparable role.
• Demonstrated knowledge of contemporary physical therapist practice, clinical education, evidence-based practice, student assessment, and professional standards.
• Experience teaching, mentoring, or supervising learners in professional or postbaccalaureate education.
• Evidence of effective communication, collaboration, organization, and the ability to develop and sustain clinical partnerships.
• Record of scholarship, service, and professional engagement appropriate to the faculty rank and appointment sought.
• Qualifications commensurate with appointment at the Assistant or Associate Professor rank on a tenure-track, tenured, or clinical track, as applicable.
Preferred Qualifications
• Earned PhD, EdD, DSc, or other academic doctoral degree relevant to physical therapist education, rehabilitation science, health professions education, or a related field. • Prior service as a DCE, assistant DCE, site coordinator of clinical education, or in a comparable leadership role within physical therapist education. • Experience with CAPTE candidacy, accreditation, self-study, reporting, program assessment, or compliance activities. • Demonstrated experience developing, administering, and assessing clinical education experiences and partnerships. • Documented professional development in educational theory and methodology, instructional design, student evaluation, clinical instructor development, and program or outcome assessment. • Experience with curriculum development, program evaluation, simulation, educational technology, or innovative models of clinical education. • Evidence of interprofessional education or practice and collaborative partnerships with health systems, community organizations, and rural or underserved clinical sites. • Active engagement in the American Physical Therapy Association or other relevant professional organizations. • Strong record of scholarship and teaching appropriate to the rank and faculty track sought. • Strategic, collaborative, and outcomes-oriented leadership; excellent written and oral communication; and demonstrated ability to expand and sustain clinical partnerships responsive to Alabama’s workforce needs.

• Record of professional activity appropriate for clinical-track faculty

• Rural background or demonstrated commitment to working with rural populations • Experience providing dental care to rural populations • Experience mentoring pre-dental or dental students • Experience in developing or contributing to curriculum refinement or educational program improvement • Experience collaborating with community partners, clinics, or health-related organizations

We seek an accomplished artist-scholar with expertise in teaching contemporary and modern dance techniques, a distinguished record of professional creative achievement, and a demonstrated commitment to excellence in undergraduate teaching within a liberal arts environment.
Job Description:
The successful candidate will teach undergraduate courses in contemporary and modern dance technique at beginning through advanced levels, choreograph an original work annually for Vassar Repertory Dance Theatre, and teach seminar and/or lecture courses that examine dance through critical, historical, cultural, and theoretical frameworks. We welcome applicants whose creative and scholarly work advances understandings of dance through diverse cultural, historical, aesthetic, and embodied perspectives. Experience with interdisciplinary artistic and scholarly collaboration is highly valued. The teaching load in the first year is the equivalent of four full credit courses, following which the load is the equivalent of five full credit courses per year, or four plus intensive work with students which typically involves directed student research.
Responsibilities will include maintaining an active creative and/or scholarly practice, mentoring and advising undergraduate students in their artistic, academic and professional development. Additionally, contribution to the curriculum development and continued growth of the department while fostering interdisciplinary collaborations within the department and across the College is expected.
Qualifications:
Candidates must have a Ph.D., MFA or equivalent professional accomplishment in Dance or a closely related field at the time of appointment with demonstrated excellence in teaching contemporary and modern dance technique at multiple levels as an academic and artist. A sustained record of professional creative work, including choreography and/or performance is also required. Candidates must also have demonstrated commitment to inclusive, equitable, and student-centered pedagogy and the ability to contribute to the intellectual and artistic life of a liberal arts college through teaching, creative practice, scholarship, and service.
Preference will be given to candidates with previous college-level teaching experience; an active professional network and sustained engagement within the contemporary and modern dance communities; experience developing collaborative projects across artistic disciplines; a record of effective student mentorship and support for students' academic, artistic, and professional growth; and experience integrating technologies such as video, photography, sound, and digital media into creative practice and/or teaching.
Application Materials:
Cover Letter and CV
Teaching Statement
Community Impact Statement (https://offices.vassar.edu/dean-of-the-faculty/positions/community-impact-statement/)
Contact information for three references who will provide reference letters upon request. Note: Candidates will be prompted for the contact information following the submission of the application.
Course evaluation material along with Syllabi of courses taught for advanced candidates
Links to videos demonstrating original choreography
Portfolio of creative work (can include published writings, choreographic documentation, selected press, or links to videos demonstrating teaching)
How to Apply:
Applications should be addressed to John Meehan and submitted online at: https://vassar.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/Vassar-External . Please contact John Meehan at jomeehan@vassar.edu with any questions. Review of applicant materials will begin on October 30, 2026 and will continue until the position has been filled. There is no guarantee that applications received after October 30, 2026 will be reviewed.

The annual base starting salary range for this position is $100,000 to $130,000 (USD). This range includes advanced Assistant Professors as well as recently tenured Associate Professors. When extending an offer of employment, Vassar College considers factors such as (but not limited to) candidate's education/training, work experience, internal peer equity, as well as market and organizational considerations. The College of Engineering (COE) at Western Carolina University (WCU) is growing!
The University has received substantial support from the North Carolina legislature to expand engineering to meet the rapidly growing needs of the region and state. Have a minimum of three (3) or more years of U.S. project-based construction industry experience.

University-level teaching experience including online/distance education.

jobs.title: Assistant Teaching Professor -- Department of Economics
jobs.description:
Assistant Teaching Professor -- Department of Economics
Position overview
Position title:
Assistant Teaching Professor of Economics
Salary range:
The current salary range for Assistant Teaching Professor is $111,400–163,200 (9-month academic year salary), however, off-scale salary and other components of pay, which would yield compensation that is higher than this range, are offered to meet competitive conditions.
Anticipated start:
July 1, 2027
Application Window
Open date: September 23, 2026
Next review date: Friday, Nov 6, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time)
Apply by this date to ensure full consideration by the committee.
Final date: Friday, Nov 6, 2026 at 11:59pm (Pacific Time)
Applications will continue to be accepted until this date.
Position description
The Department of Economics at the University of California, Berkeley, invites applications for a teaching-track position at the level of Assistant Teaching Professor, 100% time, open fields. Assistant Teaching Professors are full members of the academic senate and are eligible for Security of Employment, equivalent to tenure.
The responsibilities of Assistant Teaching Professors emphasize teaching large enrollment courses, especially at the undergraduate level, and contributing to the teaching mission of the department. The Assistant Teaching Professor would lead the pedagogical training of the Graduate Student Instructors (GSIs) and participate in the department's Undergraduate Committee, ensuring that the GSIs and Faculty are aligned in delivering the best instruction to undergraduates. Assistant Teaching Professors are also expected to maintain professional and/or scholarly achievement and activity, and to contribute to university and public service as senate faculty.
About the Department: The Department of Economics is among the largest teaching and research departments at UC Berkeley and is consistently ranked among the top five in its field worldwide. The department employs 17 departmental staff, approximately 40 ladder-rank faculty, and maintains a total academic membership of approximately 70 scholars, including joint appointments, lecturers, visiting faculty and active emeritus.
Family Friendly Policies: UC Berkeley values the family needs of faculty, including dual career couples, single parents, or those who may have taken time off for family reasons. For information about potential relocation to Berkeley, or career needs of accompanying partners and spouses, please visit the Office for Faculty Equity and Welfare's website.
Qualifications
Basic qualifications (required at time of application)
Ph.D. (or equivalent international degree) or enrolled in a PhD (or equivalent international) degree-granting program at the time of application.
Preferred qualifications
Ph.D. (or equivalent international degree) in Economics or a related field completed by date of appointment preferred.
Candidates are preferred to have demonstrated potential and/or a proven record of teaching excellence at the undergraduate level, especially in large enrollment courses, and scholarly experience in economics. It is preferred if candidates have a record and/or potential for pedagogical innovation and effective leadership, including demonstrated ability to manage large enrollment courses staffed with teams of graduate student instructors. Candidates are preferred to have experience or demonstrated commitment to professional service.
The preferred candidates for a position will have demonstrated that they are promising or established educators in economics and who are interested in a teaching-focused career. Applicants should be excited about the opportunity to teach large (400+ student) undergraduate courses and would develop and share best practices for teaching a diverse student body, particularly relevant with the rapidly changing environment for undergraduate education in the era of AI.
Application Requirements
Document requirements
Cover Letter
Curriculum Vitae - Your most recently updated C.V.
Statement of Teaching and Mentoring - Please discuss prior teaching experience, teaching approach, and future teaching interests. This can include, for example, specific efforts and accomplishments, and future plans to support the success of all students through inclusive curriculum, classroom environment, and pedagogy. Please also discuss your mentoring experiences and approach. This can include, for example, past efforts and future plans to support the success of all students, and to foster an inclusive research environment that removes barriers and promotes equitable access and advancement of the research program.
Teaching Dossier - A dossier of teaching materials that can include a selection of course syllabi; course website link(s); video(s) of your teaching (either as an attachment or linked online); created course materials such as homework assignments, projects, lecture slides, handouts and/or exams; teaching evaluations (with student comments) received either as a teaching assistant and/or as an instructor of record; peer evaluations of teaching; or other materials of your choosing that showcase your teaching excellence. There is no page limit, though make sure to highlight key achievements in the Statement of Teaching.
Statement of Professional and/or Scholarly Achievement and Activity - A statement describing your professional and/or scholarly achievements and activities, or promise of productive contributions to professional and/or scholarly activity, that would support excellent teaching, including a description of plans for future scholarship at UC Berkeley. Professional and/or scholarly activities may be related to the underlying discipline itself or to the pedagogy. Such activities should provide examples of achievement, leadership, and/or influence. Certain administrative work (e.g., of learning centers and teaching programs) and community outreach work are also relevant, as would be presentations of seminars or lectures at other institutions or professional societies, or participation in scholarly activities (e.g., summer seminars) designed to enhance scholarly expertise in relevant fields. Other records of participation in intensive programs of study - in order to be a more effective teacher and scholar, with the goal of enhancing one's teaching and scholarly responsibilities - are also relevant evidence of professional and/or scholarly activity.
Statement of University and Public Service - Please discuss specific prior and proposed academic, professional and/or public service activities. This can include, for example, participating in professional or scientific associations, serving on committees that advance department, campus or discipline goals, and conducting outreach activities that can remove barriers and increase participation of academics in your field.
Authorization to Release Information Form - An institutional reference check will be completed only if you are selected as the candidate to whom the hiring unit would like to extend a formal offer. Download, complete, sign, and upload the Authorization to Release Information form.
Reference requirements
3-5 letters of reference required
​Reference letters must be requested by the deadline to have a complete application​ in APRecruit​​, but the search committee expects to receive the letters by the deadline​, or asap afterwards.
Applicants must provide three letters of recommendation that speak to their record and/or potential for excellence in teaching and mentoring, as well as scholarly achievement (including related to instruction and pedagogy) and service. Letters that speak to an applicant's pedagogical methods, skills of presentation and exposition, or interaction with students are especially important.
Apply link:
https://aprecruit.berkeley.edu/JPF05531
Help contact: facrecruit-econ@berkeley.edu
About UC Berkeley
UC Berkeley is committed to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging in our public mission of research, teaching, and service, consistent with UC Regents Policy 4400 and University of California Academic Personnel policy (APM 210 1-d). These values are embedded in our Principles of Community, which reflect our passion for critical inquiry, debate, discovery and innovation, and our deep commitment to contributing to a better world. Every member of the UC Berkeley community has a role in sustaining a safe, caring and humane environment in which these values can thrive.
The University of California, Berkeley is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age, or protected veteran status.
For more information, please refer to the University of California's Affirmative Action and Nondiscrimination in Employment Policy and the University of California's Anti-Discrimination Policy.
In searches when letters of reference are required all letters will be treated as confidential per University of California policy and California state law. Please refer potential referees, including when letters are provided via a third party (i.e., dossier service or career center), to the UC Berkeley statement of confidentiality prior to submitting their letter.
As a University employee, you will be required to comply with all applicable University policies and/or collective bargaining agreements, as may be amended from time to time. Federal, state, or local government directives may impose additional requirements.
The University of California is committed to creating and maintaining a community dedicated to the advancement, application, and transmission of knowledge and creative endeavors through academic excellence, where all individuals who participate in University programs and activities can work and learn together in a safe and secure environment, free of violence, harassment, or discrimination. Consistent with this commitment, UC Berkeley requires all applicants for Senate faculty positions to complete, sign, and upload an Authorization of Information Release form into AP Recruit as part of their application. If an applicant does not include the signed authorization, the application will be considered incomplete, and as with any incomplete application, will not receive further consideration. Although all applicants for faculty recruitments must complete the entire application, applicants will only be subject to institutional reference checks if and when they are selected as the candidate to whom the hiring unit would like to extend a formal offer. More information is available on this website.
As a condition of employment, the finalist will be required to disclose if they are subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct.
“Misconduct” means any violation of the policies or laws governing conduct at the applicant's previous place of employment, including, but not limited to, violations of policies or laws prohibiting sexual harassment, sexual assault, or other forms of harassment or discrimination, as defined by the employer.

Job Details
Job Title: Part-Time Faculty of English
Location: Clayton State University
Regular/Temporary: Regular
Full/Part Time: Part-Time
Job ID: 303589
About Us
Located in Morrow, Georgia, Clayton State University is roughly 15 miles southeast of downtown Atlanta. The university offers employees an adaptable, collaborative environment that fosters professional and personal development.
The university is committed to having a positive impact on the State of Georgia and beyond by serving students and the community through broadening access to high-quality education and advancing workforce development. Clayton State offers multiple certificates, Associate's, Bachelor's, and Master's Degree programs, which currently enroll over 5,500 students in challenging campus and online courses.
Clayton State's main campus is situated on 214 beautiful acres in a lakeside setting just minutes from downtown Atlanta, making access to the vibrant metropolitan area swift. The Atlanta-Journal Constitution has named the university a Top Workplace in Atlanta for six consecutive years. The Chronicle of Higher Education also named Clayton State one of 79 higher education institutions across the nation in its list of 2017 Great Colleges to Work For.
Job Summary
The Department of English seeks three (3) part-time instructors to teach first-year writing (English 1101 and 1102) and assist with portfolio assessment at the Main Campus and off-site locations: Rockdale, Fayette, Henry, Clayton, and Fulton County. This position will be filled by candidates with experience in teaching first-year writing and survey of literature courses who can help with the work of the writing program, as desired. The candidate should have a Master of Arts (M.A.) in English or higher with successful experience and/or training in teaching writing.
Responsibilities
Teaching two writing courses per semester.
Assessing portfolios.
Holding office hours and being accessible to students.

Job Details
Job Title: Assistant Professor of Communication
Location: Kennesaw, Georgia
Regular/Temporary: Regular
Full/Part Time: Full-Time

About Us
For more than 60 years, Kennesaw State University has been known for its entrepreneurial spirit and sense of community. A leader in innovative teaching and learning, Kennesaw State is located just north of Atlanta and combines a suburban setting on two metro-Atlanta campuses in Kennesaw and Marietta. As one of Georgia's largest universities, Kennesaw State offers undergraduate and graduate degrees to over 50,000 students. Our high-impact research and Division I athletics also draw students from throughout the region and across the globe. A member of the University System of Georgia, Kennesaw State is a Carnegie-designated doctoral research institution (R2) committed to becoming a world-class academic institution positioned to broaden its academic and research missions and expand its scope on a local, regional, and national level.
Our university's vibrant culture, career opportunities, rich benefits, and values of respect, integrity, collaboration, inclusivity, and accountability make us an employer of choice. As part of the University System of Georgia, Kennesaw State exemplifies the power and promise of a student-centered, research-driven university. In addition, Kennesaw State supports the University of Georgia's core values of accountability, excellence, integrity, and respect. We are searching for talented people to join Kennesaw State University in our vision. For more information, visit the Kennesaw State University website.
Location
Our Kennesaw campus is located at 1000 Chastain Road NW, Kennesaw, GA 30144. Our Marietta campus is located at 1100 South Marietta Parkway, Marietta, GA 30060.
Department Information
The School of Communication & Media prepares ethical, mindful, and effective communicators who combine human skills and technical expertise to pursue fulfilling careers, lead in their communities, tell impactful stories, and grow strong relationships. We blend industry-relevant programs with forward-thinking scholarship to build understanding of the power of communication to innovate, connect, and create.
With more than 400 full-time faculty and 8,100 degree-seeking students, the Norman J. Radow College of Humanities & Social Sciences is dedicated to pioneering workforce readiness in the humanities and social sciences. By staying true to our Liberal Arts values and integrating practical knowledge and experiential learning into our curriculum, we empower our students to become responsible citizens ready for the demands of the modern workplace. The home of three schools and eight departments, the College offers more than 80 graduate and undergraduate programs of study in both traditional and interdisciplinary fields. These programs enable students to develop leadership, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills, as well as a strong sense of civic engagement.
The College is committed to the success of our students, faculty, staff and communities. We seek candidates whose experience has prepared them to fulfill that commitment and engage our students, partners, and stakeholders effectively.
Job Summary
Kennesaw State University is now accepting applications for a full-time, tenure track faculty position as Assistant Professor of Communication in the School of Communication and Media with a preferred start date of August 2027. This is a nine-month contracted position and is for work to be performed in the state of Georgia.
Responsibilities
Teach required and elective courses across the School of Communication and Media, with primary responsibilities supporting the Journalism and Emerging Media program and supplemental teaching in the Media and Entertainment program. Potential courses include Digital Media Production, Uses and Effects of Mass Media, Data Journalism, Investigative Reporting, Narrative Journalism and Fundamentals of Digital Journalism.
Develop and integrate courses in artificial intelligence and data visualization that enhance our offerings to students in the School of Communication and Media.
Teach on the Kennesaw and/or Marietta campuses, as assigned. Courses may be delivered in face-to-face, hybrid and online formats.
Teach courses of various sizes, ranging from lab skills courses in journalism to large lectures in foundations and introductory courses.
Maintain an active program of research or creative scholarship in artificial intelligence and data visualization as it relates to the field of Communication consistent with the expectations of a tenure-track faculty appointment.
Disseminate research and scholarship in appropriate, high-quality outlets.
Proactively seek external funding to support research and creative scholarship consistent with the expectations of a tenure-track faculty appointment.
Contribute expertise in data visualization and artificial intelligence to curriculum development involving the practical, critical, ethical and professional implications of emerging technologies.
Contribute service to the School, College, University and profession and collaborate with colleagues in a multidisciplinary School of Communication and Media.
Contribute, as appropriate, to professional development opportunities for students and communication professionals, community partnerships and interdisciplinary projects within the College.
Opportunities to teach graduate courses may also be available.
Teaching assignments will be based on earned degrees and SACSCOC Faculty Credentials Guidelines.
Required Qualifications
A terminal degree, or the foreign equivalent, in communication, mass communication, journalism, digital media or a closely related discipline is required at the time of hire.
Demonstrated expertise in the application of artificial intelligence to journalism, media production or other communication fields.
Documented teaching, course-development or professional experience demonstrating preparation to teach courses related to application of data visualization and artificial intelligence to communication and media professions.
Documented scholarly or creative activity demonstrating the potential to maintain an active program of research or creative scholarship.
Documented experience or training relevant to face-to-face, hybrid and online instruction, such as prior teaching, course design or formal instructional training.
Preferred Qualifications
Documented teaching, course-development or professional experience demonstrating preparation to teach courses related to digital media, journalism or media production.
Active record of quality dissemination of research in artificial intelligence and data visualization in communication and mass communication fields.
Experience in seeking external funding to support research and creative production in fields of expertise.
At least two years of professional experience in digital or broadcast media production.
Experience with data journalism, data visualization, computational methods, creative artificial intelligence, sports media production or related areas.
Evidence of excellence in teaching and student engagement, as demonstrated by teaching evaluations, peer observations, teaching awards, instructional materials or similar evidence.
Experience contributing to curriculum development involving emerging technologies and their practical, ethical and professional implications.
Required Documents to Attach
CV documenting educational background, teaching experience, research or creative scholarship and relevant professional experience
Cover Letter addressing qualifications for the position, including relevant teaching or professional experience and the applicant's research or creative scholarship agenda.
Unofficial Transcripts (Official Transcripts and Official International Course-by-Course Evaluations Due Upon Hire)
Names, phone numbers, and email addresses of at least 3 references.
Teaching Philosophy
Research Interest (A 2-page statement of research interest that breaks down your anticipated research agenda in a tenure-track role at Kennesaw State.)
Evidence of Teaching Effectiveness (A 2-page white paper that summarizes teaching evaluations, certifications that support more effective teaching, and other efforts to enhance what you bring to the classroom.) Upload as Additional Documents
Incomplete applications will not be considered.
Apply Before Date
Review of applications will begin immediately.For full consideration, please apply by October 26, 2026.

POSITION DESCRIPTION:
The Department of Statistical Sciences in the Faculty of Arts and Science at the University of Toronto invites applications for a full-time tenure stream position in the area of Data Science Computation and adjacent fields. The appointment will be at the rank of Assistant Professor with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027.
This search aligns with the University’s commitment to strategically and proactively promote diversity among our community members (Statement on Equity, Diversity & Excellence). Recognizing that Black, Indigenous, and other Racialized communities have experienced inequities that have developed historically and are ongoing, we strongly welcome and encourage candidates from those communities to apply.

Candidates must have earned a PhD degree in Statistics, Computer Science, Data Science, or a closely related discipline by the time of appointment, or shortly thereafter, with a demonstrated record of excellence in research and teaching in Data Science Computation or adjacent fields. We are seeking exceptional candidates whose research advances the theoretical and methodological foundations of computation in data science, including, but not limited to, sampling and simulation, computational inference, optimization, randomized numerical methods, and scalable algorithms for high-dimensional problems, with particular interest in statistical-computational tradeoffs, complexity, convergence, and theoretical guarantees.
The successful candidate should have experience working with, teaching, or mentoring diverse groups or diverse students is preferred. We seek exceptional candidates whose research and teaching interests complement and strengthen our existing departmental research strengths.
Candidates must provide evidence of research excellence which can be demonstrated through a record of publications in top-ranked and field relevant journals or forthcoming publications meeting high international standards; the submitted research statement; presentations at significant conferences; awards and accolades; and strong endorsements from referees of high standing.

Candidates are also expected to show evidence of a commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, and the promotion of a respectful and collegial learning and working environment demonstrated through the application materials.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
The successful candidate will be expected to establish innovative and independent research at the highest international level and to establish an outstanding, competitive, and externally funded research program.
In addition, the successful candidate will be assigned a teaching and service load.

The expected salary range is $140,000 to $190,000 CAD per annum, depending on experience. Negotiations beyond this salary range will be considered for exceptionally qualified candidates.

Description:
The Department of Anesthesia and Pain Management at Sinai Health (SH) is seeking a staff anesthesiologist for the position of Deputy Site Head of Anesthesia at Mount Sinai Hospital (MSH). The successful candidate must be eligible for an academic appointment at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor in the Department of Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine, Temerty Faculty of Medicine, at the University of Toronto. The anticipated start date will be July 1, 2027, or one which is mutually agreed upon.
Mount Sinai (442 beds) is an acute care hospital and home to the largest high-risk obstetric center in Canada. Surgical services include general surgery, gynecology, otolaryngology, urology, oral and maxillofacial surgery, dentistry, orthopedics, and ophthalmology. All surgical programs have significant oncology components. Opportunities for practice in acute and chronic pain are also available.
The Deputy Site Head will be responsible for managing the day-to-day activities of the clinical and academic department. The Deputy Site Head will also be an integral member of the departmental and institutional leadership teams, as well as the Practice Plan Executive Committee. As such, the incumbent will be involved in developing departmental strategies and aligning the site’s activities with these strategies. The successful candidate will receive 1-day per week protected time for these administrative duties. Additional protected time will be provided according to a merit-based system for educational and research activities. The successful candidate will provide anesthetic care throughout the SHS clinical programs. Clinical supervision and teaching of students, residents, and fellows is expected. On-call services will be provided in rotation.
The successful candidate must have proven leadership and clinical skills and evidence of demonstrated excellence in education or research. The successful candidate must have a medical degree, postgraduate fellowship training, Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada certification in anesthesia (or equivalent), and be eligible for licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario.
Compensation for clinical activities will be based on clinical billings through the practice plan depending on the amount of clinical and administrative/academic work performed; compensation will be commensurate with qualifications and experience and within the usual range for an anesthesiologist in the Province of Ontario, which exceeds $200,000 CAD per annum.

Head, Department of Anesthesia and Pain Management, SH-UHN, WCH, CAMH, KEI

200 Elizabeth Street, EN3-463, Toronto, ON M5G 2C4, Canada

jobs.title: Associate/Assistant Professor in Intelligent Sensing and Network Communication
jobs.description:
(Ref. No.: IOTSC/ISNC/AAP/04/2026)
The University of Macau (UM) is a comprehensive research-oriented public university of international standing in the Macao Special Administrative Region, which is located in the western part of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA), one of the world s fastest-growing hubs for technology and innovation. UM is ranked 145th in the Times Higher Education World University Rankings and 267th in the QS World University Rankings. With a scenic campus of approximately 1 km2 on Hengqin island, UM has achieved significant progress in the past decade as evidenced by its rising international repute, state-of-the-art teaching and research facilities, and the establishment of three State Key Laboratories in microelectronics, Chinese medicine, and internet of things for smart city. Committed to supporting Macao s economic diversification and the development of the Guangdong-Macao In-Depth Cooperation Zone in Hengqin, UM actively advances frontier research and develops interdisciplinary programmes in a range of strategic areas, including precision oncology, advanced materials, regional oceanography, artificial intelligence and robotics, data science, cognitive and brain science, and economics and finance. Leveraging its 4-in-1 model of education and residential college system, UM provides all-round undergraduate education, nurturing talent to support social and economic development of Macao and the wider GBA. As part of its continued development, UM is establishing a new campus in the Cooperation Zone in Hengqin, setting the stage for the university to become the first higher education institution in Macao to extend operations into the Cooperation Zone. Scheduled to commence operations in 2028, the Cooperation Zone campus will usher in the one university, two campuses model, further strengthening UM s capacity for teaching and research. With unprecedented growth and development, UM offers a wide range of opportunities for high-calibre talents at all levels to achieve their career goals. The university uses English as its working language and primary medium of instruction.
The Institute of Smart City Technologies (ISCT) invites applications for the position of Associate/Assistant Professor, who will also be a joint faculty member in the Faculty of Information Science and Computing (FIC), in the following disciplines:
IoT infrastructure and devices (sensors, embedded systems, etc.)
Sensing technologies
IoT security and privacy-enhancing technologies
IoT communications and networking
Institute of Smart City Technologies - ISCT
The Institute of Smart City Technologies (ISCT), established in 2026 as an independent academic unit of the University of Macau, advances smart-city development through education, research, innovation, and technology transfer. Working closely with the State Key Laboratory of Internet of Things for Smart City (IOTSC), ISCT conducts research in IoT, artificial intelligence, big data, and smart-city engineering. Through interdisciplinary collaboration, talent cultivation, and industry partnerships, ISCT develops innovative solutions to promote urban sustainability, enhance quality of life, and support innovation-driven development in Macao and the Greater Bay Area. More details about the Institute of Smart City Technologies are available from https://isct.um.edu.mo/.
Faculty of Information Science and Computing - FIC
As part of a strategic expansion, UM recently established five science and technology faculties through the restructuring of part of its existing faculties. In which, the Faculty of Information Science and Computing (FIC) emerges from a thoughtful and forward-looking reorganization of the former Faculty of Science and Technology, reflecting our university s commitment to sharper academic focus, greater interdisciplinary synergy, and a more agile response to the rapidly evolving landscape of information science and intelligent technologies. The Faculty brings together six interconnected departments Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Electronic and Communication Engineering, Microelectronics, Robotics, and FinTech & Business Intelligence. More details about the Faculty of Information Science and Computing are available from http://fic.um.edu.mo/.
Qualifications
A PhD degree in Computer Science, Electrical and Electronic Engineering or related disciplines;
A distinguished record of internationally-recognized research and scholarship;
Demonstrable competence in communication; and
English is the working language, while knowledge in Chinese/Portuguese will be an advantage.
The selected candidate is expected to assume duty as soon as possible.
Remuneration
A taxable annual remuneration starting from MOP1,052,800 (approximately USD129,980) for the position of Associate Professor and MOP855,400 (approximately USD105,600) for the position of Assistant Professor will be commensurate with the successful applicants academic qualification and relevant professional experience. The current local maximum income tax rate is 12% but is effectively around 5% - 7% after various discretionary exemptions. Apart from competitive remuneration, UM offers a wide range of benefits, such as medical insurance, provident fund, on campus accommodation/housing allowance and other subsidies. Further details on our package are available at: https://career.admo.um.edu.mo/learn-more/.
Application Procedure
Applicants should visit https://career.admo.um.edu.mo/ for more details, and apply ONLINE. Review of applications will continue until the position is filled. Applicants may consider their applications not successful if they are not invited for an interview within 3 months of application.
Human Resources Section, Office of Administration
University of Macau, Av. da Universidade, Taipa, Macau, China
Website: https://career.admo.um.edu.mo/; Email: vacancy@um.edu.mo
Tel: +853 8822 8577; Fax: +853 8822 2412
The effective position and salary index are subject to the Personnel Statute of the University of Macau in force. The University of Macau reserves the right not to appoint a candidate. Applicants with less qualification and experience can be offered lower positions under special circumstances.
***Personal data provided by applicants will be kept confidential and used for recruitment purpose only***
** Under the equal condition of qualifications and experience, priority will be given to Macao permanent residents**

Successful candidates are expected to contribute to undergraduate and postgraduate teaching, curriculum development, and student mentorship, while establishing internationally competitive research programs.

jobs.description:
Johns Hopkins University is making a major investment in data science and the exploration of artificial intelligence. The Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering is embarking on an aggressive hiring effort for multiple tenure-track positions.
Our search includes multiple tracks in Electrical and Computer Engineering and artificial intelligence, including:
AI Hardware and Systems, including AI accelerators, computer architecture for machine learning, energy-efficient computing, hardware-software co-design, memory systems, and photonics for AI hardware.
Sensing, Signal Processing, and Communications for AI, including AI for wireless and communication systems, machine learning for signal processing, sensor fusion, statistical learning for noisy physical systems, and uncertainty-aware inference.
Autonomy, Control, and Cyber-Physical Systems, including adversarial robustness, learning-based control, robot perception and control, safe reinforcement learning, and secure and reliable cyber-physical systems.
Other areas of Electrical and Computer Engineering related to artificial intelligence, including signal processing, sensing, inference, learning for dynamical systems, and other emerging AI-related ECE areas.
We are particularly interested in interdisciplinary researchers whose work spans applications in areas such as national security, societal safety, healthcare, clinical care, neuroscience, communications, sensing, robotics, and other domains of importance to the University's mission. Faculty will have the opportunity to participate in Johns Hopkins University's Data Science and AI Institute and benefit from its unparalleled computational infrastructure and interdisciplinary environment.
The Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering has 35 full-time tenured and tenure-track faculty members, 6 research faculty, 3 teaching faculty, 150 PhD students, over 120 MSE students, and 180 undergraduate students.
QualificationsThe candidate must hold a Ph.D. in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or a related field and will be expected to contribute to the growth of the Electrical & Computer Engineering program, develop an independent research program, secure research funding, and teach courses in the electrical and computer engineering area.

A cover letter describing the candidate's principal research expertise
A curriculum vitae

Position Summary:
The Department of Economics & Finance at the University of North Carolina Asheville, a public liberal arts and sciences university, seeks qualified applicants with expertise in Finance for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant professor position that will begin in the fall semester of 2027. The successful candidate must have earned a Ph.D. in Finance, Economics, or closely related discipline prior to July 1, 2027 and will be expected to teach 12 contact hours per semester (typically three or four classes); establish their scholarly activities that involve undergraduates; and engage in service to the institution, the community, and the profession.
The department is open to a variety of field specializations as we seek to grow the Finance program at UNC Asheville as part of a new School of Business, Economics and Professional Studies that will serve our region and beyond. The department is particularly interested in individuals with expertise to teach courses and conduct research in financial management, health care finance, quantitative finance, financial economics, fintech, impact finance, or financial data analytics.
Individuals with demonstrated excellence in teaching, a strong commitment to undergraduate education, and a well-developed plan to establish an active research program that involves mentoring students are strongly encouraged to apply. In addition, the successful candidate will be expected to contribute to the core curriculum and engage in departmental and university-level service.
UNC Asheville values interdisciplinary perspectives, often incorporated in teaching within the core curriculum. Multidisciplinary perspectives are welcomed, as is pedagogical collaboration with colleagues from across the campus. UNC Asheville has also been a national leader in undergraduate research for over 30 years, and over 67% of our students graduate each year having been involved in this important learning experience. The University fully embraces the idea of mentored undergraduate research being one of the highest forms of teaching, and the institution values success in this facet of a faculty member’s work. Therefore, the successful candidate for this position must be able to articulate a clear vision for a sustainable, highly productive, and preferably externally funded scholarly activity that includes undergraduates. Successful candidates should also have the propensity to teach in a multitude of modalities, from face-to-face to online/asynchronous format.
Applications for this position should be submitted electronically at https://jobs.unca.edu. Complete applications require a cover letter, curriculum vitae, statement of teaching philosophy that includes interest in or potential for interdisciplinary teaching outside of the department, statement of planned scholarship and creative activities, undergraduate transcripts, and graduate transcripts. Each applicant should also request three letters of reference to be sent separately that address the candidate’s written, verbal and interpersonal skills; ability to teach and mentor undergraduate students; and potential to develop successful, externally funded scholarly activities. Review of applications will begin October 12 and continue until the position is filled. Inquiries may be directed to Finance Search Chair, econsearch@unca.edu, Department of Economics & Finance.
The University of North Carolina Asheville is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race; color; ethnicity; religion; sex; pregnancy; sexual orientation; gender identity or expression; national origin; age; disability; genetic information; political affiliation; National Guard or veteran status, consistent with applicable federal, state and local laws, regulations, and policies, and the policies of The University of North Carolina.
Qualifications:
A PhD in Finance, Economics, or related field with expertise in Finance earned prior to July 1, 2027 is required for this position. The successful candidate must be able to demonstrate through application materials and in the interview that they have demonstrated excellence in undergraduate education, a concrete research agenda that includes the mentoring of undergraduate students, a desire to contribute to general education requirements, and have interests in interdisciplinary work across the university.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Title: Professor, 9 Month Salaried - School of Dance
Location: Tallahassee, FL
Regular/Temporary: Regular
Full/Part Time: Full-Time

Department
School of Dance
Responsibilities
The Florida State University School of Dance invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track Open Rank Faculty in Dance with expertise in Dance Science, Dancer Health and Wellness, and evidence-informed approaches to dancer training. We seek a collaborative scholar, educator, and mentor whose work bridges scientific inquiry, embodied practice, and creative exploration in ways that advance the preparation and well-being of dancers. Situated within our nationally recognized Dancer Training Program, this position offers a distinctive opportunity for an individual whose expertise may span areas such as applied science, performance research, pedagogy, somatic practices, rehabilitation, conditioning, creative scholarship, or interdisciplinary inquiry, while maintaining a clear commitment to optimizing dancer development through research-informed practice. The successful candidate will join a dynamic community of faculty, staff, and students dedicated to innovation, excellence, and the evolving future of dancer training.
Teaching
The successful candidate will contribute to the School's nationally recognized Dancer Training Program through teaching that reflects expertise in dance science, dancer health and wellness, and evidence-informed approaches to training.
Teaching courses such as Dance Conditioning, Dance Kinesiology, Science of Dance Training, Dance Coaching, Research in the Dance Sciences, and related topics.
Contributing specialized instruction in areas aligned with the candidate's expertise, such as Pilates, Gyrotonic, Yoga, Strength and Conditioning, Somatic Practices, Motor Learning, Injury Risk Management, Rehabilitation-Informed Training, Dance Technique, and other movement-based practices.
Developing innovative courses and learning experiences that integrate scientific inquiry, embodied practice, creative exploration, and emerging approaches to dancer development.
Research and Creative Scholarship
The successful candidate will maintain an active research and/or creative scholarship agenda that advances the preparation, performance, health, and well-being of dancers.
Conducting research related to dancer health, wellness, performance optimization, conditioning, pedagogy, injury risk management, motor learning, and related areas of dance science.
Disseminating scholarship through peer-reviewed publications, presentations, and other professional activities and venues with national and international reach.
Engaging in applied, practice-based, and creative forms of inquiry that connect research with studio, classroom, laboratory, rehearsal, or performance settings.
Contributing to the continued evolution of dance science through interdisciplinary, collaborative, and innovative approaches to research and artistic practice.
Service
The successful candidate will contribute to the shared governance and mission of the School of Dance through service to the program, university, and profession.
Serving on the Dance Conditioning and Wellness Committee and supporting initiatives within the School's Movement Training Laboratory.
Contributing expertise to programs and initiatives that promote dancer health, wellness, and performance excellence.
Participating in School, College, and University governance through committee work and other service assignments determined through faculty governance processes and in consultation with the Chair.
Engaging in professional service activities that support the broader fields of dance science, dancer training, and higher education.
Mentoring and Student Development
The successful candidate will mentor undergraduate and graduate students as artists, scholars, researchers, and movement practitioners.
Advising students pursuing interests in dance science, dancer health and wellness, movement training, performance coaching, or related fields.
Mentoring student research, creative scholarship, and practice-based inquiry.
Guiding students in the application of evidence-informed approaches to performance preparation, training, recovery, and injury-risk reduction.
Supporting students' professional development and preparation for careers in academic, artistic, clinical, research, or interdisciplinary settings.
Contributing to an environment of student success through mentoring that extends across teaching, scholarship, service, and community engagement.
Qualifications
Doctoral degree from an accredited institution or the highest degree appropriate in the field of specialization from an accredited institution in one of the dance sciences or a related field with an emphasis on working with dancers.
Evidence of scholarly, creative, or applied research activity related to dancer development, health and wellness, performance optimization, pedagogy, movement training, or closely related areas.
Demonstrated ability to contribute to a collaborative academic environment and to work effectively with faculty, staff, and students in advancing initiatives related to dancer training, health, and wellness.
Demonstrated commitment to evidence-informed practice and the integration of research, embodied knowledge, and teaching.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience teaching courses related to dance science, dancer health and wellness, movement training, conditioning, kinesiology, performance preparation, pedagogy, coaching, or related fields.
Experience teaching, coaching, training, or facilitating movement-based practices such as Pilates, Gyrotonic, Yoga, Strength and Conditioning, Somatics, Motor Learning, Injury Risk Management, Rehabilitation-Informed Training, Dance Technique, or other approaches that support dancer development and well-being.
Active research, creative scholarship, or applied professional practice that advances understanding of healthy and effective dancer training.
Experience mentoring undergraduate and/or graduate students in research, creative inquiry, professional practice, or career pathways related to dance science, dancer health and wellness, and movement training.
Demonstrated ability to bridge scientific inquiry, embodied practice, and artistic exploration in teaching, scholarship, or professional work.
Familiarity with quantitative, qualitative, mixed-methods, and/or practice-based research approaches relevant to dancer training and performance, including experience with small-N and within-subject research designs.
Other Information
The College of Fine Arts at Florida State University is dedicated to fostering artistic excellence, creative exploration, and scholarly inquiry across a variety of disciplines. Our renowned faculty and staff educate and empower students to become visionary performers, artists, educators, art historians, designers, curators, art therapists, researchers, and arts administrators who shape the future of the visual arts, healing arts, performing arts, and design. Through passionate teaching, community engagement, innovative research, and artistic practice we enrich lives, elevate artistic expression, and inspire positive change and well-being in society.
Dance has been included in Florida State University’s offerings for over 90 years, with a major degree program for more than 60 of those years. It has been recognized as a leader among college dance programs. Graduates of our programs include dancers, teachers, scholars, and leaders in companies, schools, universities, and art organizations in the United States and abroad. Montgomery Hall is one of the best dance facilities in the nation. The Maggie Allesee National Center for Choreography (MANCC) is an internationally recognized dance research center and part of the School of Dance. This unique and visionary institute brings a steady stream of prominent and emerging dance artists to campus to create and develop the work that the rest of the world will experience in years to come. Add to this mix an esteemed faculty and talented, highly motivated students, and it is easy to see why we are excited for what is to come.

One of the nation's elite research universities, Florida State University preserves, expands, and disseminates knowledge in the sciences, technology, arts, humanities, and professions, while embracing a philosophy of learning strongly rooted in the traditions of the liberal arts and critical thinking. Founded in 1851, Florida State University is the oldest continuous site of higher education in Florida. FSU is a community steeped in tradition that fosters research and encourages creativity. Job Details
Job Title: Research Faculty - 12 Month Salaried (Open Rank) – Applied Superconductivity Center (NHMFL)
Location: Tallahassee, FL
Regular/Temporary: Regular
Full/Part Time: Full-Time
Job ID: 63582
Department
Applied Superconductivity Center – National High Magnetic Field Laboratory
Responsibilities
This position will be responsible for conducting research in High Temperature Superconducting magnet technology driving the highest possible fields with superconducting magnets, a core mission of the MagLab, as well as important for the fusion industry, particle accelerators, and medical imaging sectors. Duties will include support in our successful Little Big Coil program which recently set a world record DC field of 50 Tesla, including modeling electromechanical properties of conductors and coils, as well as building and testing those coils under extreme operating conditions near or at their failure points.
This position holder will be one of the key personnel for continuing development of our torque magnetometer and other forefront experimental probes, as well as working as a core team member to develop in-field reel-to-reel characterization technology for ReBCO coated conductors.
Additional duties include participation in outreach activities by interacting with the public and explaining various ASC capabilities during tours and open house. Interact with numerous technical visitors from domestic and international laboratories and industries.
The successful applicant will demonstrate an ability to carry out specialized, high level engineering tasks to develop magnets, cryostats, electronic instruments, characterization apparatus (including magnetometers, transport probes and sample holders) and other high field measurement facilities at the ASC.
ASC operates in a very flexible and interactive fashion, and the candidate is expected to work collaboratively with others and to attend and present at regular meetings at which results, strategy and the work of others are constructively discussed.
Qualifications
PhD required in Physics, Applied Physics, Materials Science, Engineering or equivalent experiential background with appropriate publication and conference presentation record. We envisage someone with at least three years post-PhD experience in the field.
Must be able to understand instrumentation controls and data acquisition systems, troubleshoot instruments, and a drive to design the best strategy for solving technical issues. As these systems operate in cryogenic environments, sound experience with the operation of cryogenic systems is a requirement.
An understanding of superconducting microstructures, as well as standard light and electron microscopy tools is also expected. The candidate will work closely with various undergraduate and graduate students and positive mentoring skills are expected.

jobs.title: Full/Associate/Assistant Professor in Stem Cell Biology and Regenerative Medicine
jobs.description:
(Ref. No.: FMD/SCBRM/FAAP/09/2026)
The University of Macau (UM) is a comprehensive research-oriented public university of international standing in the Macao Special Administrative Region, which is located in the western part of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA), one of the world s fastest-growing hubs for technology and innovation. UM is ranked 145th in the Times Higher Education World University Rankings and 267th in the QS World University Rankings. With a scenic campus of approximately 1 km2 on Hengqin island, UM has achieved significant progress in the past decade as evidenced by its rising international repute, state-of-the-art teaching and research facilities, and the establishment of three State Key Laboratories in microelectronics, Chinese medicine, and internet of things for smart city. Committed to supporting Macao s economic diversification and the development of the Guangdong-Macao In-Depth Cooperation Zone in Hengqin, UM actively advances frontier research and develops interdisciplinary programmes in a range of strategic areas, including precision oncology, advanced materials, regional oceanography, artificial intelligence and robotics, data science, cognitive and brain science, and economics and finance. Leveraging its 4-in-1 model of education and residential college system, UM provides all-round undergraduate education, nurturing talent to support social and economic development of Macao and the wider GBA. As part of its continued development, UM is establishing a new campus in the Cooperation Zone in Hengqin, setting the stage for the university to become the first higher education institution in Macao to extend operations into the Cooperation Zone. Scheduled to commence operations in 2028, the Cooperation Zone campus will usher in the one university, two campuses model, further strengthening UM s capacity for teaching and research. With unprecedented growth and development, UM offers a wide range of opportunities for high-calibre talents at all levels to achieve their career goals. The university uses English as its working language and primary medium of instruction.
The Faculty of Medicine (FMD) was established in August 2026 through the expansion and restructuring of the former Faculty of Health Sciences. The Faculty's educational mission is delivered through five academic departments: the Department of Biomedical Sciences, Department of Clinical Medicine, Department of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences, Department of Public Health and Medicinal Administration, and Department of Medicinal Food and Nutrition Sciences. Stem Cell Biology and Regenerative Medicine is one of the key strategic research focuses of FMD.
The Faculty of Medicine (http://fmd.um.edu.mo/) invite applications for the position of Full, Associate, or Assistant Professor in Stem Cell Biology and Regenerative Medicine.
Successful candidate will be expected to provide academic and strategic leadership in stem cell biology and regenerative medicine, develop internationally recognizable research programmes, and foster interdisciplinary collaborations within the University and with leading institutions worldwide. Working closely with the current faculty members in this field, the candidate will play a key role in shaping UM's development, strengthening its research capacity, building high-impact research teams, and advancing translational research. The candidate will also contribute to the Faculty's educational mission through teaching, postgraduate supervision, and academic programme development. Through the excellence in research, teaching, and services, the successful candidate will help strengthen UM's position as a leading centre for basic and translational research, innovation, and talent development.
Qualifications
A doctoral degree in biological sciences, biotechnology, health sciences, medicine, or a related discipline. Candidates are expected to have well-recognized track record in developmental biology, stem cell biology, regenerative medicine, and/or cell and gene therapy, demonstrated through publications in leading international journals. Competence also includes success in obtaining competitive research funding, editorial board memberships, and invited presentations at major international conferences. Preference will be given to candidates whose research is either clinically relevant or has great potential for clinical translation. For Assistant Professor, it is preferable to have three years or above of postdoctoral training. Senior candidates should have demonstrated strong academic leadership, experience in leading interdisciplinary research initiatives, and the ability to build internationally competitive research programmes and mentor junior researchers.
The selected candidate is expected to assume duty in 2026/2027.
Remuneration
A taxable annual remuneration starting MOP1,250,200 (approximately USD154,350) for the position of Full Professor; MOP1,052,800 (approximately USD129,980) for the position of Associate Professor and MOP855,400 (approximately USD105,600) for the position of Assistant Professor will be commensurate with the successful applicants academic qualification and relevant professional experience. The current local maximum income tax rate is 12% but is effectively around 5% 7% after various discretionary exemptions. Apart from competitive remuneration, UM offers a wide range of benefits, such as medical insurance, provident fund, on-campus accommodation/housing allowance and other subsidies. Further details on our package are available at: https://career.admo.um.edu.mo/learn-more/.
Application Procedure
Applicants should visit https://career.admo.um.edu.mo/ for more details, and apply ONLINE. Applicant should submit a cover letter in which the preferred position(s) is specified, along with a detailed Curriculum Vitae. Review of applications will continue until the position is filled. Applicants may consider their applications not successful if they are not invited for an interview within 3 months of application.
Human Resources Section, Office of Administration
University of Macau, Av. da Universidade, Taipa, Macau, China
Website: https://career.admo.um.edu.mo/; Email: vacancy@um.edu.mo
Tel: +853 8822 8589; Fax: +853 8822 2412
The effective position and salary index are subject to the Personnel Statute of the University of Macau in force. The University of Macau reserves the right not to appoint a candidate. Applicants with less qualification and experience can be offered lower positions under special circumstances.
***Personal data provided by applicants will be kept confidential and used for recruitment purpose only***
** Under the equal condition of qualifications and experience, priority will be given to Macao permanent residents**
